issue.title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Keep the HyperConnection padding rows deterministic across reloads
issue.body:
## Overview

`GatedResidual` packs the HyperConnection down projection and its block-inject weight into one `MergedColumnParallelLinear` whose output is padded to 16 rows (`pad_size = (-(hc_lowrank + hc_count)) % 16`). No checkpoint tensor carries that padding shard, and its output is discarded, so nothing ever wrote it: the rows kept whatever `torch.empty` in `create_weights` returned.

A weight update under `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` has to reproduce a cold start bit for bit. A dummy-started lane fills **every** parameter before the first update, padding included, and nothing rewrote those rows afterwards. The two HyperConnection parameters of every layer then never matched a cold start again, so the direct-reload equivalence oracle fails even though the model outputs are unaffected (the padding rows are split off and dropped in `forward`).

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #66002 (models opt in; refuse known-silent paths) *gates* undeclared paths, it does not fix this one.
- #65526 (`refill_derived` for mHC broadcast) rewrites four sites — DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 NVIDIA+AMD, Muse Spark ROCm, FlashInfer/b12x sinks. `qwen4_exp` is not among them.
- #65799 (an update must deliver everything cold start loaded) catches a *missing* tensor. Here every tensor is delivered; the missing shard is alignment padding that no checkpoint carries by design.
- #65347 (bitwise cold-start e2e) is the oracle that catches this, not a fix.
- #66461 excluded the NVIDIA padding shard from the loaded-shard check. Its AMD counterpart is handled separately in #66813. This PR makes the padding bytes deterministic across reloads.

## What changed

- New `PaddedMergedColumnParallelLinear` (in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/hyperconnection.py`): records the padding row range, zeroes it at construction, and reports the parameter through `padding_fill_params()` so `begin_direct_reload` zero-fills it before each update loads its shards.
- `GatedResidual` in the NVIDIA and AMD variants use it for `input_mix_weight_down_block_inject`.
- `test_hc_padding_shard_is_not_expected_from_checkpoints` now fills dummy values, calls the real `record_checkpoint_layout` and `begin_direct_reload`, and loads the two real shards with distinct values. It asserts zero padding at construction, after begin, and after loading, and checks the loaded shard values exactly.

## Validation

One H20-3e, 1 GPU, vllm `0.33.0rc1.dev1073+g821851eab`, torch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA IPC weight transfer, `--enforce-eager`, a reduced Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (1 layer, 8 experts). Oracle is the one from vllm-ascend PR 16959: normal startup load of the payload == first live update == second live update, plus a per-parameter SHA256 comparison through `POST /weight_checker`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| direct | FAIL — 2 parameters differ after both updates (`layers.0.attn_hyper_connection.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject.weight`, `layers.0.mlp_hyper_connection.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject.weight`) | **PASS** — 357/357 digests equal, signatures equal |
| layerwise | PASS — 0 mismatches | PASS — 0 mismatches |

The cold start itself is reproducible (two reference runs: 0 mismatches), so the difference was not allocator noise.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2, the pinned revision) pass on the four files.

## Latest review follow-up

Merged upstream main at `65711a1617` and replaced the test's manual `weight.zero_()` with the real direct-reload entry points. The AMD checkpoint-shard declaration is excluded here and proposed separately in #66813.

The pinned Ruff check and format pre-commit hooks passed on the follow-up's two changed files; `git diff upstream/main --check` passed. Full pre-commit stopped while downloading its Node environment.

## Not verified

- The GPU results above were collected before the latest review follow-up and merge with main.
- The updated focused pytest attempt stopped while importing `tests/conftest.py` on Windows: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'uvloop'`. No test cases ran. Further runtime tests were deferred at the submitter's explicit request.
- The AMD variant was not exercised on an AMD GPU.
- The full test suite and CI steps have not been rerun for this follow-up.

AI assistance was used to prepare and review this change.

comment.body:
## Verification for this PR

This reproduces the bug on the unpatched commit and shows it gone with the patch, using the same
oracle as the earlier direct-reload work: **normal startup load of a payload == first live update ==
second live update**, plus a **per-parameter SHA256** comparison (so a reload that keeps the generated
tokens but not the bytes still fails).

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| commit | `821851eab0` (`0.33.0rc1.dev1073+g821851eab`), patch overlaid as a package overlay on the same build |
| GPU | 1× NVIDIA H20-3e (143 GiB), `--enforce-eager`, TP=1 |
| transfer | CUDA IPC (`--weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"ipc"}'`), `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` / `layerwise` |
| model | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, reduced through `--hf-overrides` to `{"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 1, "num_experts": 8, "layer_types": ["linear_attention"]}}` |
| payload | 362 checkpoint tensors, 3.43 GiB, deterministic per-name seeds; written as a checkpoint so the reference is a real startup load |
| torch | 2.14.0+cu130 |

### Results

| lane | before the patch | with the patch |
|---|---|---|
| `direct` | **FAIL** — 2/357 parameters differ after both updates; signatures equal | **PASS** — 0/357 differ, signatures equal |
| `layerwise` | PASS — 0/357 | PASS — 0/357 |
| cold start ×2 | PASS — 0/357, identical signatures | PASS — 0/357 |

The two parameters that differed are exactly the ones this PR touches:

```
dp0:pp0:pcp0:tp0:language_model.model.layers.0.attn_hyper_connection.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject.weight
dp0:pp0:pcp0:tp0:language_model.model.layers.0.mlp_hyper_connection.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject.weight
```

Update latency was 7.24 s / 7.45 s before and 7.36 s / 7.36 s after, i.e. the extra zero-fill is not
measurable at this scale.

**The failure is not noise.** Running the cold-start lane twice on the same checkpoint gives 0/357
differences and identical signatures, so the reference bytes are reproducible; before the patch the
two lanes disagreed deterministically on the same two parameters on every update.

### Test code

The in-repo unit test is the one this PR extends:

```python
def test_hc_padding_shard_is_not_expected_from_checkpoints(dist_init) -> None:
    """Checkpoints carry only the down and block-inject rows, not the padding."""
    hc = GatedResidual(HyperConnectionConfig())
    assert hc.pad_size > 0
    linear = hc.input_mix_weight_down_block_inject

    def padding_rows() -> torch.Tensor:
        return linear.weight[hc.hc_lowrank + hc.hc_count :]

    # The padding rows must be deterministic: a weight update is compared
    # against a cold start bit for bit, and nothing ever loads these rows.
    assert not padding_rows().any()
    # A direct reload zero-fills the parameter at `begin` through this
    # declaration, so a dummy-started lane cannot keep its dummy values here.
    assert linear.padding_fill_params() == ["weight"]

    # Dummy start, then `begin`, then the update's two real shards.
    with torch.no_grad():
        linear.weight.fill_(1.0)
    with torch.no_grad():
        linear.weight.zero_()
    for shard_id, rows in ((0, hc.hc_lowrank), (1, hc.hc_count)):
        weight = torch.ones(rows, hc.hyper_hidden_size)
        weight.shard_id = shard_id
        set(linear.load_weights([("weight", weight)]))
    assert linear.pop_missing_shards() == []
    assert not padding_rows().any()
```

The end-to-end oracle (trimmed to the lane sequence; the full script builds the payload from the
checkpoint metadata and runs the two modes as separate jobs):

```python
overrides = {"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 1, "num_experts": 8,
                             "layer_types": ["linear_attention"]}}
common = ["--hf-overrides", json.dumps(overrides), "--tokenizer", repo,
          "--dtype", "bfloat16", "--max-model-len", "1024",
          "--tensor-parallel-size", "1", "--trust-remote-code", "--enforce-eager"]

# 1. Independent oracle: a server that loads the payload at normal startup.
with server(model=str(ckpt_dir), args=common) as ref_url:
    ref_sig = signature(ref_url)          # text + token logprobs for 2 prompts
    ref_ck = checksums(ref_url)           # POST /weight_checker {"action": "checksum"}

# 2. Live lane: dummy start, payload over IPC, reload mode under test.
with server(model=repo,
            args=[*common, "--load-format", "dummy",
                  "--weight-transfer-config", '{"backend": "ipc"}'],
            env={"VLLM_RELOAD_MODE": mode}) as live_url:
    start_sig, start_ck = signature(live_url), checksums(live_url)
    engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
        IPCTrainerInitInfo(rank=0),
        client=HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient(live_url),
        source=payload_source,            # same tensors that were written to ckpt_dir
    )
    signatures, digests = [], []
    for _ in range(2):
        engine.send_weights()             # start -> load -> finish
        signatures.append(signature(live_url))
        digests.append(checksums(live_url))

assert start_sig != ref_sig                                  # the transfer must be observable
assert signatures[0] == signatures[1] == ref_sig             # text + logprobs
assert digests[0] == digests[1] == ref_ck                    # every parameter, byte for byte
```

### Reproduce

```bash
sbatch run.slurm qwen3.8-flash direct    full   # before: FAIL, 2 mismatches; after: PASS
sbatch run.slurm qwen3.8-flash layerwise full   # PASS both ways
sbatch run.slurm qwen3.8-flash direct    ref2   # cold start twice: 0 mismatches
```

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2, the pinned revision) pass on the four files. The rest
of the suite was not run; this comment covers the focused CUDA e2e and the unit test only.

Happy to attach the full harness (payload construction, digest collection, job wrapper) if you want
to run it on other Qwen4Exp variants.

issue.title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Import each packed NPU IPC export once
issue.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Packed NPU IPC transfers currently rebuild and then release the producer's shared mapping once per chunk. The producer, however, exports its reusable staging buffer only once and sends the same rebuild arguments with every chunk. Since torch pairs one IPC export with one consumer rebuild/release cycle, a multi-chunk transfer drives the producer-side refcount negative. Once the staging buffer is dropped, it cannot be reclaimed, leaking one `packed_buffer_size_bytes` allocation per update on every producer rank.

This adapts the import-cache fix merged upstream in vLLM [#51259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51259) to the Ascend NPU consumer:

- add an NPU implementation of the upstream `PackedBufferImporter` that reuses one rebuilt mapping across chunks from the same export;
- wire one importer into each `NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine` and release it through the inherited `finish_weight_update()` / `shutdown()` lifecycle or when a new export replaces it;
- add regression coverage for one import across multiple chunks, fresh payload reads through the cached mapping, cleanup, reuse after cleanup, replacement between exports, and a failed rebuild;
- update the existing receive test to assert that the engine passes its shared importer to the packed consumer.

The unpacked path, wire format, public APIs and configuration are unchanged. This is a focused alternative to the importer portion of the broader, currently conflicting [#18085](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18085), not a replacement for that PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Packed NPU IPC live weight updates no longer retain a producer staging buffer after each update. There is no new API or configuration. A release-note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU source harness with the real engine, importer, packing and loading code; only configuration, logging and hardware primitives were stubbed: **125 passed**.
- The same regression case against the pre-fix source fails at the second import with `2 != 1`, confirming it covers the reported lifecycle.
- Eight-card Ascend host (225), real eight-layer BF16 checkpoint, TP4/DP2/EP8, eight producer ranks, packed buffer 4352 MiB, `max_tokens=8`:
  - structured run report: **passed**;
  - both `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`: **4/4** outputs, tokens and finite token logprobs identical before and after the packed weight update, **8/8 total**;
  - checkpoint manifest and sampled parameters were consistent across the eight workers;
  - the update client exit did not reproduce `Producer process has been terminated before all shared NPU tensors released`.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, `py_compile` and `git diff --check` passed.

The real-host run completed the update and post-update inference checks. Normal post-update service shutdown was not completed because the shared-host occupancy guard detected unrelated NPU processes and stopped the test container; that shutdown path remains covered by the unit regression but was not exercised end to end in that run.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage:** Repeated chunks, replace-on-next-export, repeated cleanup and a failed rebuild are covered.
- [x] **Regression test:** The new test fails against the pre-fix source.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage:** A rebuild failure preserves the existing mapping, which is released by cleanup.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests:** Tests exercise the actual importer lifecycle and payload freshness rather than only checking call counts.
- [ ] **Performance impact:** This removes repeated IPC opens and closes; no standalone benchmark was run.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

comment.body:
Verified this change on real Ascend NPU hardware. Here is what I ran and observed.

## Environment

- Ascend NPU, CANN `25.5.1`, firmware `7.8.0.2.212`
- `torch 2.10.0+cpu` / `torch_npu 2.10.0.post4`
- vLLM `0.26.0+empty` @ `84030bbe3d`, which already carries the upstream `PackedBufferImporter` (vLLM #51259)
- Source under test: this PR at head `2c941ca24`

## Unit tests — `tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_npu_ipc_engine.py`

| source under test | result |
|---|---|
| PR head | **19 passed** |
| the two source files reverted to the merge base `b91f8335d`, new tests kept | **3 failed** |

The 3 failures are both parameters of `test_packed_export_imported_once_with_fresh_payload_and_release` plus `ImportError: cannot import name 'NPUPackedBufferImporter'`. So the new coverage really does fail against pre-fix source, as claimed.

One caveat about how I ran it: in this environment the repo's `tests/ut/conftest.py` fails to import for reasons unrelated to this PR (`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rms_norm.py` imports `kernel_launcher`, which the vLLM checkout here does not provide — a vLLM/vllm-ascend version skew). I therefore ran the module from an isolated directory with a `conftest.py` that only pre-imports `vllm.model_executor.model_loader`, so the repo's `_patch_reload_module()` fake no longer shadows the newer `reload` API. No assertion in the test file was modified.

## Real-hardware refcount reproduction

The Ascend driver rejects importing a shareable handle inside the exporting process, so this needs two processes: the producer exports one staging buffer once via `reduce_tensor`, and a child process consumes it as several chunks.

| consumer behaviour | rebuilds per export (3 chunks) | leaked per update |
|---|---|---|
| rebuild + release per chunk (pre-fix) | 3 | **67,109,376 B (64 MiB)**, cumulative and unreclaimable across updates |
| one `NPUPackedBufferImporter` shared by all chunks (post-fix) | **1** | **0**, allocator returns to baseline |

The pre-fix run also ends with `Producer process has been terminated before all shared NPU tensors released` (`NPUIPCTypes.cpp:23`), i.e. the symptom described in the description. In both modes the mapping still aliases the producer's buffer, so bytes written between chunks are still read fresh — the clone in `packed_npu_ipc_consumer` keeps the loaded tensors independent.

## replace-on-next-export

One long-lived importer serving two exports (2 chunks each, 32 MiB per staging): **2 rebuilds total**; dropping export A reclaimed its 32 MiB once B replaced the cache entry, `close()` reclaimed B, **0 bytes leaked**. A and B carry different ref-counter handle args, so the `tuple(list_args)` key does distinguish exports.

## Static

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the three changed files. The head merges cleanly onto current `main`, which still has no `PackedBufferImporter` under `vllm_ascend/`.

Not covered here: the 8-card TP4/DP2/EP8 end-to-end rerun, and the post-update shutdown path.

## Two small notes

- `release_notes/fragments/20740.yaml` is absent at head — `2c941ca24` removed what `6d499c11a` added — while the description still says a fragment is included. Probably worth restoring before merge.
- The assertion inside the fake `rebuild()` (`assert args[-1] == f"export-{len(imports) + 1}"`) fires first on pre-fix source and reports `'export-1' == 'export-2'`, masking the clearer top-level `assert len(imports) == 1`. Folding that check into the top-level assertion would make the failure self-explanatory. Non-blocking.

review.body:
## Overall Review

The overall design of Exact Expert Offloading is reasonable. The CPU HostExpertStore, fixed NPU resident slots, and runtime expert mapping provide a good foundation for exact MoE expert offloading while maintaining compatibility with ACL Graph replay.

However, there are several correctness and robustness issues that should be addressed before merging.

### 1. [P1] Validate FullExpertPool Layout Compatibility Across Layers

**File:** `expert_offload_manager.py`

The shared `FullExpertPool` is allocated using only the first expert binding:

```python
self.full_pool.allocate(next(iter(self.bindings.values())))
```

However, the same pool is subsequently reused by all MoE layers.

This implicitly assumes that all layers have identical physical expert layouts, including:
- Number of local experts.
- W13/W2 physical storage sizes.
- Quantization formats and dtypes.
- Scale tensor layouts and storage sizes.

This assumption is not explicitly validated. In particular, `TorchExpertTransfer.copy_experts()` calculates destination offsets using the source layer's `expert_bytes`. If another layer has a different physical expert size, this could result in incorrect writes or even out-of-bounds memory access.

**Suggestion:**

Validate the physical storage layout of all bindings during manager initialization. If the layouts are incompatible, either fail early with a clear error or allocate separate FullExpertPools for different layout signatures.

For the currently supported models, explicit compatibility validation should be sufficient.

### 2. [P1] Handle Partial Expert Transfer Failures Safely

**File:** `transfer.py` / `expert_offload_manager.py`

`load_resident()` updates `slot_to_expert` and the expert mapping only after the transfer operation completes.

However, `copy_experts()` performs multiple asynchronous copies sequentially. If one copy fails after previous copies have succeeded, some resident slots may already contain new expert weights while the mapping still describes the old experts.

For example:
- Expert 4 is successfully copied into Slot 0.
- Copying Expert 5 into Slot 1 fails.
- The mapping remains unchanged.
- A subsequent request may incorrectly treat Slot 0 as still containing Expert 0 and skip reloading it.

This can result in silently using incorrect expert weights if execution continues after the failure.

**Suggestion:**

Define an explicit failure policy for partially completed transfers:
- Invalidate all potentially modified slots and force them to be reloaded; or
- Mark the binding/manager as failed and prevent subsequent forward execution until recovery.

Please also add a failure-injection test where the second expert copy fails, verifying that subsequent execution cannot reuse stale residency metadata.

### 3. [P2] Explicitly Validate Supported Quantization Schemes

**File:** `expert_offload_manager.py` / `method.py`

The current adapter checks whether the native method belongs to `AscendFusedMoEMethod`, but this base class can represent multiple quantization schemes.

However, `MXFPExpertAdapter` assumes a specific set of parameters:

```python
tensor_names = (
    "w13_weight",
    "w2_weight",
    "w13_weight_scale",
    "w2_weight_scale",
)
```

This adapter is specifically designed for W4A8-MXFP and W8A8-MXFP. Other schemes may require additional parameters, such as weight offsets, or use different physical layouts.

**Suggestion:**

Explicitly validate the supported quantization types and required parameter layouts during binding initialization. Unsupported schemes should fail early with a descriptive error instead of failing later during weight processing or transfer.

### 4. [P2] Avoid Unnecessary D2H Synchronization During Prefill

**File:** `expert_offload_manager.py`

The current implementation extracts selected expert IDs from `topk_ids` before checking whether the request is in the prefill phase:

```python
selected_expert_ids = set(
    topk_ids.detach()
    .to(device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
    .reshape(-1)
    .tolist()
)

use_full_pool = (
    manager.has_prefill
    or len(selected_expert_ids) > self.num_slots
)
```

When `manager.has_prefill` is already true, the FullExpertPool path is guaranteed to be selected. Therefore, copying the entire `topk_ids` tensor to CPU and constructing a Python set is unnecessary.

For long-context prefill, this introduces avoidable D2H synchronization and CPU-side overhead for every MoE layer.

**Suggestion:**

Check the prefill condition first and only extract expert IDs when resident-slot selection is actually required:

```python
if manager.has_prefill:
    use_full_pool = True
else:
    selected_expert_ids = set(
        topk_ids.detach()
        .to(device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
        .reshape(-1)
        .tolist()
    )
    use_full_pool = len(selected_expert_ids) > self.num_slots
```

### 5. Additional Test Coverage

The current tests cover the main residency, transfer, eager, and ACL Graph execution paths. However, I recommend adding the following cases:

- Multiple MoE layers with different expert storage layouts.
- Partial asynchronous transfer failures and subsequent recovery.
- Explicit rejection of unsupported quantization schemes.
- Actual A5 hardware execution of the Graph Replay and Eager Fallback integration tests.

Please also ensure that the latest performance benchmarks are rerun against the current PR head, since the existing benchmark results may not reflect the latest implementation.

---

## Final Assessment

The overall architecture is sound and worth pursuing. The fixed resident-slot design and preprocessed host weight storage are particularly suitable for exact expert offloading with ACL Graph replay.

However, I consider the first two issues important correctness concerns. They should be addressed before merging to avoid potential memory corruption or incorrect expert execution.

The remaining items are mainly compatibility validation and performance improvements.

### Review Summary

The implementation looks correct and is consistent with the upstream vLLM scheduling behavior. Both `BalanceScheduler` and `DyntraLBScheduler` correctly propagate `has_sync_kv_loads` to `SchedulerOutput`.

I have the following suggestions:

**1. Add test coverage for asynchronous KV loads (P2)**

The current tests only cover synchronous external KV loads (`load_kv_async=False`) and requests without external KV hits.

Please extend the tests to cover:
- Asynchronous external KV loads (`load_kv_async=True`): `has_sync_kv_loads` should remain `False`.
- Synchronous external KV loads (`load_kv_async=False`): `has_sync_kv_loads` should be `True`.
- Mixed batches containing both synchronous and asynchronous KV loads: `has_sync_kv_loads` should be `True`.

Please apply the same test coverage to both `BalanceScheduler` and `DyntraLBScheduler`.

**2. Consider backporting the fix to release branches**

The original issue also affects the vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0 release line. The corresponding release branches still lack this bookkeeping logic, while upstream vLLM v0.30.0 already supports `has_sync_kv_loads`.

Please consider backporting this fix to the relevant release branches to ensure the original issue is resolved for existing users.

**3. Optional: Add end-to-end validation (P3)**

An integration test verifying that synchronous KV loading starts before model forward would provide stronger confidence in the fix. This is optional since the worker-side execution ordering is already handled by upstream vLLM.

**Overall:** The production code changes look correct, and I don't see any obvious implementation issues. I recommend adding the missing asynchronous and mixed-load test cases before merging. The release backport can be handled separately.

issue.body:
## Overview

Move the six allocator helpers into `CuMemAllocator` as private, overridable methods so subclasses can reuse its allocation lifecycle methods.

## Claims

- Make `_create_and_map`, `_unmap_and_release`, `_create_cpu_backup`, and `_release_cpu_backup` private static methods, with internal calls dispatched through `self`.
- Make `_get_pluggable_allocator` and `_use_memory_pool_with_allocator` private instance methods that use the existing retained callbacks.
- Update both poisoned-remapping test helpers to replace and restore the class static method correctly.

## Validation

The human submitter reviewed the initial migration and published [CUDA verification for head `47849d33b5`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66518#issuecomment-6737469715), covering the allocator/sleep suites, HTTP sleep interfaces, subclass dispatch, and a baseline comparison. The report explicitly leaves ROCm, XPU, and downstream Ascend unverified. These device results are submitter-reported; the agent's Windows host has PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and cannot reproduce them. Agent-side checks for the `_` prefix revision included an exact rename-only AST comparison, actual module/constructor/descriptor checks, applicable commit hooks, and mypy on both test files.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -v
```

The subsequent review fix documents the subclassing contract and returns the pluggable allocator directly. Ruff, formatting, applicable commit hooks, source compilation, real module import/construction, and an AST comparison limited to the docstring and immediate-return simplification passed. Device tests were not rerun for this follow-up. The preceding head `47849d33b5` also has a [published device verification report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66518#issuecomment-6737469715).

Agent-side checks:

- Ruff 0.17.2 lint/format, typos, and all ten applicable repository Python check hooks passed, including Buildkite test tethering.
- Module import, the real allocator constructor, compilation of all three changed files, and whitespace checks passed.
- An AST comparison against the base verified unchanged implementations for the four static operations and only callback lookup / helper dispatch changes elsewhere.
- Pinned mypy 1.20.2 passed both test files. The allocator reports three host-environment errors: Unix-only `mmap(flags=...)` / `MAP_PRIVATE`, and the existing nullable library-name annotation. Checking the original file with `--shadow-file` reproduced the same three errors.

The commit hooks ran with documented exclusions: mypy was checked separately as above; the filename check was performed natively because Bash cannot run in this Windows environment; the Docker graph hook is inapplicable to these files; informational/signoff Bash hooks were omitted, and the commit's `Signed-off-by` was verified directly. Hooks for unchanged file types were also excluded to avoid installing unrelated tool environments. This is not a claim that an unmodified full pre-commit run passed.

Local pytest collection failed in `tests/conftest.py` on missing `uvloop`; no device or model evaluation was run by the agent. The existing Basic Correctness CuMem and Sleep Mode CI steps, including AMD mirrors, already select both suites and include the changed paths in their source dependencies.

## Details

Module-level calls bypass subclass methods of the same name. Dispatching through `self` provides the requested extension points for users such as vllm-ascend's `CaMemAllocator`. Pool creation already consumes instance callbacks, so those redundant parameters are removed.

The module-level helper exports are removed. The six underscored helpers are documented subclass extension hooks, not direct public entry points. The class docstring lists all six and explicitly treats changes to their names or signatures as breaking changes. XPU's independent helpers, direct CUDA memcpy calls, synchronization, backup ownership, ROCm-specific handles, singleton behavior, and sleep/wake policies are unchanged. Complete Ascend lifecycle reuse remains follow-up work.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR for this migration after searches for `CuMemAllocator staticmethod`, `cumem inheritance`, `use_memory_pool_with_allocator`, and the broader cuMem area. Merged #64630 introduced the backup implementation; open #64465 fixes wake-up copy retry and #65772 fixes asleep-allocation backup release. Neither migrates these helpers. No issue is claimed as fixed.

AI assistance was used for implementation, test updates, host validation, and this description. The submitting human confirmed line-by-line review and relevant device test execution for the initial migration; follow-up validation is scoped above.

### H20 verification: sleep-mode public interfaces, allocator extension points, and the two changed suites

Verified **`47849d33b52593f638782630b46bcac4ac5ec59d`** (PR head; it merges `main` at `1648e80a6a`, and the delta against that tip is exactly the 3 files in this PR).

#### Environment

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Cluster / node | SGP H20e cluster, **2 x H20-3e** (143 GB each), Slurm `--gres=gpu:2`; PR job `7261` on `vllm-sgp-h20-01`, baseline job `7275` on `vllm-sgp-h20-02` |
| Compiled extensions | per-commit wheel of the merge base `821851eab0`: `vllm-0.33.0rc1.dev1073+g821851eab`, **torch 2.14.0+cu130** (CUDA 13), from `wheels.vllm.ai` |
| Code under test | that wheel's compiled package + `vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py` copied from the PR head over it (pure-Python change, no C++/CUDA delta) + the PR-head `tests/` tree |
| Baseline | the same wheel, the same commands, the merge-base `cumem.py` (prepended package copy) and the merge-base copies of the two test files |

#### 1. Public sleep APIs over HTTP (PR head)

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-sleep-mode` with `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`, greedy (`temperature=0, max_tokens=8`), then every externally visible sleep interface. Output before sleeping: `" I'm a student, and I'm"`.

```
PASS /is_sleeping is false before sleep
PASS /sleep?level=1 -> 200 {'status': 'sleeping', 'level': 1}
PASS /is_sleeping is true at level 1
PASS POST /wake_up?tags=weights -> 200 {'status': 'sleeping', 'tags': ['weights']}
PASS partial wake reports 'sleeping'        # wake_up returns False until every tag is back
PASS POST /wake_up?tags=kv_cache -> 200 {'status': 'awake', 'tags': ['kv_cache']}
PASS level-1 cycle preserves greedy output
PASS /sleep?level=2 -> 200 {'status': 'sleeping', 'level': 2}
PASS collective_rpc reload_weights -> 200 {'results': [None]}
PASS level-2 wake reports 'awake'
PASS level-2 cycle preserves greedy output
PASS /sleep?level=0 -> 200, /release_kv_cache_memory -> 200 {'status': 'kv_cache_released'}
PASS /is_sleeping is true after level 0 + release
PASS level-0 release cycle preserves greedy output
PASS /sleep?level=3 rejected with 400
PASS release without a pause is rejected (500, engine error surfaced, server stays up)
PASS untagged /wake_up reports 'awake'
PASS server still serves after all cycles
PASS 3 x repeated level-1 sleep/wake preserve greedy output
ALL 36 ENDPOINT CHECKS PASSED   (total 116 s)
```

Baseline job: the same script, `ALL 36 ENDPOINT CHECKS PASSED` (110 s).

The offline API (`LLM.sleep(level=0|1|2)`, `LLM.wake_up(tags=...)`, `LLM.release_kv_cache_memory()`, `engine.is_sleeping()`, `collective_rpc("reload_weights")`, `AsyncLLMEngine.sleep/wake_up`) is driven through the same paths by the suites in section 3.

#### 2. The refactor's actual claim: subclass dispatch

`CuMemAllocator` was subclassed the way a downstream allocator would be (override every moved helper, install it with `CuMemAllocator.instance = Sub()`, then drive it through `get_mem_allocator_instance()`, the entry point the engine uses): pool allocation -> `sleep(offload_tags=("weights",))` -> `wake_up()` -> free -> `cudagraph_pool()` -> discard/wake.

PR head: every hook is dispatched through the subclass; data survives byte-exact.

```
hook calls: {'_create_and_map': 3, '_create_cpu_backup': 1, '_get_pluggable_allocator': 4,
             '_release_cpu_backup': 1, '_unmap_and_release': 4,
             '_use_memory_pool_with_allocator': 3}
PASS every hook dispatched through the subclass -- missing=[]
```

Baseline: the same script passes functionally, but the overrides are **never invoked** - the merge-base calls the module-level functions directly. That is the behavior this refactor changes, and it is consistent with the module-level names being removable:

```
PASS base code bypasses subclass overrides -- calls={}
```

#### 3. Changed suites, PR vs baseline (same command, same job shape)

```
PYTHONPATH=... python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --import-mode=importlib -rA --no-header \
  tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py \
  tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py
```

| suite | PR head | merge-base baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` | **22 passed** (175 s) | 22 passed (158 s) |
| `basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py` | **15 passed, 1 failed\*, 1 skipped** (870 s) | 15 passed, 1 failed\*, 1 skipped (850 s) |
| `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` re-run with the toolchain on `PATH` | **1 passed** (225 s) | 1 passed (75 s) |

\* `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` failed **identically on both revisions** with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ninja'` raised from `flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py:433 run_ninja`: the test venv contains `ninja`, but it is not on `PATH` (the venv is not activated). Re-running only that test with `$VENV/bin` and `/usr/local/cuda/bin` on `PATH` passes on both revisions, after flashinfer JIT-builds its comm/sampling modules. The single skip is also revision-independent: `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool_aiter_fused_ar_group_quant` (ROCm/AITER only).

TP=2 was really exercised: `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` and `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool[custom-ar-tp2]` were selected (2 GPUs held), not skipped. The cumem suite includes `test_level2_discards_ordinary_tensor_with_weights_tag`, one of the two tests updated to patch `CuMemAllocator._create_and_map`; the other one, `test_deep_sleep_fp8_kvcache_with_undefined_remap`, passes in the sleep-mode suite.

#### Pre-commit and DCO

- `bash $HOME/vllm-shared/scripts/run-precommit.sh <repo> HEAD^` on a repo holding exactly this PR's 3-file delta: **exited 0**. `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `check-test-tethering`, mypy for the oldest supported Python, SPDX headers, docstring style, root lazy imports, forbidden imports, no-new-`torch.cuda`, and the rest of the applicable hooks passed; hooks for other file types or with unavailable toolchains (`cargo`/`node`/`go`) had nothing to check.
- DCO: every commit in the PR range carries a matching `Signed-off-by: Ronald1995 <ronaldautomobile@163.com>`, and GitHub's `DCO` app reports **pass** on this head.

#### Not verified

- **ROCm and XPU**: the AITER test is ROCm-only, so ROCm's zero-on-wake path and `xpumem.py` (independent helpers, untouched here) were not run.
- **Rust frontend** (`rust/src/server/src/routes/sleep.rs`, changed on `main` inside the merged range): not exercised; the Python server path was used.
- **Downstream projects** that subclass the allocator (e.g. vllm-ascend's): not run here; only the in-repo subclass pattern above. Note the six module-level helpers are *removed*, not just renamed - an out-of-tree `from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import create_and_map` (or any of the other five) would break. Nothing in this repo or its docs imports them any more.
- **Full CI**: only the two changed suites plus the endpoint e2e above, not the wider Buildkite set.

AI assistance was used for this verification (harness, scripts, and this comment). Job logs live on the cluster under `~/vllm-tasks/pr66518/logs/`.

review.body:
## Review: NPU verification of the `_ranks_kernel` change

I reproduced this on a lab **Atlas A3** (`ascend910_9382`, 24 AI core / 48 vector core per die, **192 KB UB**) with **`triton-ascend==3.2.2`** — the version pinned in `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` and installed by the CI workflows. The 950DT + Triton-Ascend 3.6.0 setup in the PR description is newer than what the project currently supports, and that gap is exactly where things break.

**The `>=` change is correct, but the padding guard does not compile on A3 — as written this cannot be merged.**

### 1. `>=` is the right contract — confirmed

- Upstream `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logprob.py::_ranks_kernel` uses `n += tl.sum((logits >= x)...)` in both `v0.32.0` and main `24420b7a`, and `vllm/v1/sample/ops/logprobs.py::batched_count_greater_than` returns `(x >= values).sum(-1)` despite its name. So the reference is `>=`, 1-based.
- Measured on NPU with the kernel extracted verbatim from `main` and from this PR head (same launcher/args as `compute_topk_logprobs`, `BLOCK_SIZE=8192`): for argmax / runner-up / two-way top tie, `>` gives `[0, 1, 0]` and `>=` gives `[1, 2, 2]`; on random rows the two differ by exactly 1. Your tie-multiplicity table reproduces.

### 2. The padding defect is real

With `>=` and no guard: vocab `1519` and a `-inf` selected logit → `8192`; vocab `20000`, two rows → `24576` instead of `20000`. Matches your stage B, so the extra guard is justified (upstream has the same latent issue).

### 3. Blocker: `valid & (logits >= x)` overflows UB on A3

```
loc(".../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/logprob.py":90:0): error: Failed to run BiShengHIR pipeline
loc(".../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/logprob.py":90:0): error: ub overflow, requires 1573632 bits
while 1572864 bits available! (possible reason: tiling basic block is too large or block number
is more than what user expect due to multi-buffer feature is enabled ...)
```

`1572864 bits` = 192 KiB, `1573632 bits` = 192.02 KiB — the guard is **96 bytes over** the budget. Three independent repros on the same host:

| kernel under test | compiles on A3 / triton-ascend 3.2.2 | `test_compute_topk_logprobs.py` |
|---|---|---|
| A — `>` (this PR's base) | yes | 4 params fail vs a `>=` reference |
| B — `>=`, no guard | yes | 5 pass, 1 fail (padding case) |
| C — `>=` + `valid &` (**this PR**) | **no — UB overflow** | **6 failed** |
| D — `>=` + `tl.minimum(sum, vocab_size)` | yes | 6 passed |

- `pytest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_compute_topk_logprobs.py` on this head → **6 failed**, all `MLIRCompilationError` at `logprob.py:90`, cold triton cache, deterministic.
- Reproduced with the kernel source extracted verbatim and driven by a standalone launcher (no `vllm` import), so it is the kernel body, not the harness.
- With only the `>=` change (no guard) the same harness compiles and runs, so the mask is what tips it over: it materialises two extra 8192-lane predicates (`vnot` + `vand`).

The pre-PR kernel is already at ~99.5 % of the 192 KB UB, so **any** additional per-lane buffer in this loop will fail, and `BLOCK_SIZE=8192` is pinned by the caller. Consequence: every `compute_topk_logprobs` call raises at compile time on A3 (A2 almost certainly too — same 192 KB UB — but I only had an A3 to test). The nightly suite runs this file on A2/A3, so this lands as a red nightly, and as a broken logprob path as soon as the kernel is actually bound (see 5).

### 4. Suggested fix: clamp the scalar instead of masking the compare

```diff
             n_vec = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.int32)
             for i in range(0, vocab_size, BLOCK_SIZE):
                 block = i + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
-                valid = block < vocab_size
-                logits = tl.load(row_ptr + block, mask=valid, other=float("-inf"))
-                # Rank counts entries at or above the sampled logit; padding is
-                # -inf, which also satisfies `>=` when x is -inf.
-                n_vec += (valid & (logits >= x)).to(tl.int32)
-            n = tl.sum(n_vec)
+                logits = tl.load(row_ptr + block, mask=block < vocab_size, other=float("-inf"))
+                n_vec += (logits >= x).to(tl.int32)
+            # Padding lanes are -inf, which only satisfies `>=` when x is -inf;
+            # in that case every real lane counts too, so the true rank is exactly
+            # vocab_size and clamping the over-count restores it.
+            n = tl.minimum(tl.sum(n_vec), vocab_size)
```

With only this change, **the PR's own test file passes 6/6** on the same A3 host, including both new tests. It is exact, not a band-aid: padding lanes are `-inf` and can only be counted when `x == -inf`, and then every real lane also satisfies the comparison, so the true rank is exactly `vocab_size`; for `x > -inf` no padding lane is counted and the sum is already `<= vocab_size`, so the clamp is a no-op. (Same NaN caveat as the mask: a NaN real lane would not be counted.)

If you'd rather keep an explicit mask, it needs to be free of the extra 8192-lane predicate buffer, otherwise it will not fit on A2/A3.

### 5. Smaller notes

- On the vLLM versions CI builds against (`v0.32.0` and main `24420b7a`), `sampler`, `prompt_logprob` and `rejection_sampler` import and call **`compute_topk_scores`**. `patch_triton.py:44-45` assigns `X.compute_topk_logprobs = ...`, which does not rebind that callee, so today the Ascend `_ranks_kernel` is reached only by the nightly test and the upstream kernel runs instead (I checked it on NPU: it compiles and already returns `>=` ranks, padding quirk included). #19153 mentions aligning the name. This does not invalidate the fix — it is still groundwork — but it does affect the "user-facing change" claim in the description, and it means the compile failure will move into the production path the moment the kernel is bound.
- `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/topk_log_softmax.md` documents `_ranks_kernel`; please add the rank contract (count of entries `>= x`, 1-based) and how padding is handled.
- Module-level `pytestmark`, the `>=` reference in the existing test, the trimmed docstrings and the release-note fragment all look good.

Environment note: the container I used has a vLLM checkout older than this PR's base, so `vllm_ascend.ops.triton` does not import (`vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup.kernel_launcher` is missing there). I ran the file with `--noconftest` plus a stub for that one import; the stub does not touch the ranks kernel or the UB accounting, and repros 2–4 above do not import `vllm` at all.

issue.title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B prefill TTFT regression: host ACLNN workspace/tiling is not reused
issue.body:
## Summary

On Atlas 800T A3, with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8, TP=2, MTP=3 and ACL Graph enabled, the MRV2 model runner is **25.4% slower than MRV1 on prefill TTFT** for `batch=4, prompt_len=2048, max_tokens=1`. The regression is reproducible and is not caused by NPU computation: the NPU op time is actually 3.8% lower on MRV2, while the host-side ACL API time is 35.6% higher. The extra host time comes from per-call `aclnnMatmulGetWorkspaceSize` / `MatMulV2_Tiling` / `InplaceCopy` workspace lookups that MRV1 does not perform.

This is filed as a related issue for the Qwen3.6 MRV2 adaptation task. It is an explained regression, not an unexplained one.

## Environment

- vLLM / vLLM-Ascend: 0.30.0, Qwen compatibility adaptation `qwen-v030@6b7590693ce8`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8, revision `1a118d717bcbd59480f4a110fe22181d21711b4d`
- CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7
- Atlas 800T A3, TP=2, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, ACL Graph (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), prefix caching disabled

## Observed result

Measured in one session, same container, warmup 4, measured 12:

| runner | TTFT median | TTFT p25 | TTFT p75 | prefill tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MRV1 | 0.7866 s | 0.7578 s | 0.8048 s | 2615.5 |
| MRV2 | 0.9867 s | — | — | 2084.7 |
| delta | **+25.44%** | | | **-20.3%** |

The MRV1 interquartile range is only 6%, so the difference is not run-to-run noise. An earlier independent measurement showed 28.9%, same order of magnitude.

## Root cause evidence

Torch profile of the same configuration, grouped by op type and by host ACL API:

| dimension | MRV1 | MRV2 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| NPU op total time | 861,404 us | 828,909 us | **-3.8%** |
| host ACL API total time | 1,282,342 us | 1,740,359 us | **+35.6% (+457 ms)** |

Top host-side contributors:

| API | MRV1 | MRV2 |
|---|---|---|
| `aclnnMatmulGetWorkspaceSize` | 0 calls, 0 us | **1080 calls, 104,356 us** |
| `MatMulV2_Tiling` | 0 calls, 0 us | **1912 calls, 54,906 us** |
| `aclnnInplaceCopyGetWorkspaceSize` | 368 calls, 4,384 us | **2948 calls, 47,732 us** |

MRV1 performs zero `GetWorkspaceSize` / `Tiling` lookups during the measured window, i.e. it reuses cached workspace and tiling information. MRV2 re-resolves them on every MatMul. The ~457 ms host delta is consistent in direction and magnitude with the ~200 ms TTFT delta.

## Reproduction

1. Serve the model with MRV2 enabled (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) and the configuration above, MRV1 as the control (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`).
2. Send 4 concurrent requests with `prompt_len=2048`, `max_tokens=1`, twice as warmup and twelve times as measurement.
3. Compare TTFT median and the per-API host times from the torch profiler export.

## Impact

- Prefill-dominated workloads see a double-digit TTFT regression on MRV2 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
- Decode and NPU-bound paths are not affected; NPU op time is slightly better on MRV2.

## Suggested direction

- Reuse the ACLNN workspace/tiling cache across steps in the MRV2 dispatch path instead of calling `GetWorkspaceSize` and `Tiling` per MatMul.
- Check whether MRV1's matmul path benefits from a prebuilt op descriptor that MRV2 bypasses.

## Related

- #20153 — Qwen3.6 MRV2 adaptation task (Qwen dense + MoE support, precision/performance parity). The precision side is reported separately; this issue covers only the prefill performance regression.

issue.title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B batched MTP is not batch-invariant: identical prompts in one batch diverge (MRV1 and MRV2)
issue.body:
## Summary

On Atlas 800T A3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8 with `qwen3_5_mtp` and two concurrent prompts is not reproducible within either MRV1 or MRV2. Both runners exceed the decode tolerance on the second prompt and both eventually diverge on token identity; on the first prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta stays within tolerance on both runners. With a single sequence in the batch the same prompt passes at 1.21e-06 and is byte-identical across cold starts. With two identical prompts in one batch, each runner produces two different final token sequences from index 13 onward, so the batch itself is not self-consistent for either runner. A single MRV1 run is therefore not a stable correctness baseline for batched MRV2, while the MRV2 kernel path itself shows no numerical regression.

This should be tracked as a shared batched speculative-decoding issue, not as evidence that an isolated MRV2 kernel is solely responsible.

## Environment

- vLLM / vLLM-Ascend: 0.30.0, with the local Qwen compatibility adaptation `qwen-v030@6b7590693ce8`
- Model revision: `1a118d717bcbd59480f4a110fe22181d21711b4d`
- CANN 9.2.1; torch 2.10.0; torch-npu 2.10.0.post7
- TP=1, FP16, W8A8, `qwen3_5_mtp`, one speculative token, seed 1234
- Two prompts, 24 output tokens, eager mode; graph+MTP also fails separately

## Expected behavior

Repeated cold starts of the same runner should satisfy the repository logprob comparison rules: prefill atol 0.0689 and decode atol 0.1378. Note that the harness applies the prefill tolerance only to the first generated token's logprob, so this is a narrow prefill check rather than a full prefill comparison. MRV1/MRV2 should then be compared under the same rules.

## Actual behavior

- Serial offline generation and batched generation without MTP pass the MRV1/MRV2 comparison.
- Batched MTP fails across MRV1/MRV2 in eager and graph modes.
- Single-sequence control: running the second prompt alone (`QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_OFFSET=1`, batch=1, MTP=1, eager, 24 tokens) passes. Two independent cold starts produce byte-identical JSON (both md5 `5deaa85f8e28c86ab8a4c22369df3546`), MRV1 and MRV2 token IDs are identical, and the maximum logprob delta is 1.21e-06; the within-runner delta is 0.0 for both runners. This localizes the defect to batched (batch>1) speculative decoding, not to the MRV2 kernel path.
- Identical-prompt batch control: submitting the same prompt twice in one batch (`QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_OFFSET=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_REPEAT=2`) fails within each runner. The two final token sequences are identical up to index 12 and diverge at index 13 (one copy emits `100606`, the other continues with `113895`). Since the inputs are identical, the divergence can only come from per-batch state, not from prompt content or accept-count heterogeneity. A heterogeneous two-prompt batch reproduces the same failure.
- Time-step trace shows the two requests are not synchronized: one copy finishes prefill earlier and runs 1–2 positions ahead, so the batch mixes prefill and decode. Logprob deltas taken from same-timestep snapshots are therefore contaminated by the position skew and are not usable as an error metric; the final-sequence divergence at index 13 is the valid observation.
- The cross-runner comparison operates on final token sequences and therefore remains valid; it reports 0.1676 in the homogeneous batch and 0.3020 in the heterogeneous batch. It is, however, not sensitive to the batch-level divergence, so the primary probe is the final token sequence of two identical requests in one batch.
- Independent no-probe cold starts also fail within each runner:
  - MRV1 A/B: the first prompt diverges at token 14; before that divergence the same-token logprob delta is at most 0.0386, i.e. within tolerance. The second prompt keeps identical token IDs but has four same-token logprob points above tolerance, up to 0.2473 (1.8x atol).
  - MRV2 A/B: prompts diverge at tokens 18 and 22. On the first prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta is 0.1294 (within tolerance); on the second prompt it is up to 0.3880 (2.8x atol) before divergence.
  - The "fails on both runners" claim is therefore driven by the second prompt; the first prompt stays within tolerance until its first token divergence.
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` was explicitly enabled in both engine logs, but the cross-runner comparison still fails. On the second prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta reaches 0.6634 (4.8x atol), so batch invariance alone does not restore agreement.
- Disabling shared-expert overlap is not a workaround: the second prompt still exceeds tolerance, and its divergence-point cross-lookup delta grows to 3.1767 (vs 1.7524 in the clean baseline). That 3.1767 is a cross-distribution value at the divergence point and is not comparable to the 0.6634 pre-divergence same-token value; under the pre-divergence same-token view the no-overlap delta is actually lower (0.2370). The conclusion is "not a fix", not "makes it worse".

## Isolation evidence

- Actual scheduled draft token IDs and positions are identical for the first ten GDN steps; the first scheduling mismatch appears later.
- Prefill metadata, cache indices, state dtype (`float32`), state stride, sequence lengths and scale match.
- With the original cache index layout preserved, the FP32-state fused recurrent implementation is bitwise-identical to itself across eight replays for each runner (`to_previous.max_abs_diff = 0.0`). Its comparison against the recorded output reports `max_abs_diff = 0.0` together with `cosine = 0.99991`, which is internally inconsistent; exact reproduction of the recorded output is therefore not established. These data support determinism under a fixed input, not engine-level reproducibility or the absence of recurrent-operator sensitivity.
- Disabling MTP makes the batched comparison pass in our local control runs, and eager+MTP fails, so the issue is not limited to graph replay. The no-MTP control file is not yet attached to this report.
- The batch=1 control above passes at 1.21e-06 with two byte-identical cold starts, so the Qwen3.6 MRV2 adaptation does not introduce a numerical regression by itself; the failure requires more than one sequence in the batch.
- Because identical prompts in one batch already diverge, the defect is a batch-level self-consistency problem shared by MRV1 and MRV2, not a runner-to-runner numerical difference. This also explains why `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not help: that switch addresses reduction order, while the observed divergence is consistent with per-sequence state or cache-index handling.
- `enable_prefix_caching` is ruled out: rerunning the identical-prompt batch with prefix caching disabled still produces two different final token sequences, with the first divergence moving to tokens 10/19 instead of token 13. The batch-level divergence is therefore not caused by shared prefix blocks.
- The original `recurrent_gated_delta_rule` cannot be used as a kernel-side control: with fp32 state it fails inside `fla_npu` at `aclnnRecurrentGatedDeltaRuleGetWorkspaceSize` with error `161002`, which is why the adaptation routes fp32 state to `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule`. A kernel-side A/B has to be done by state tracing rather than by reverting the path.
- State tracing moves the root cause earlier than GDN. In the identical-prompt batch, the two copies already differ in the **layer-0 input hidden states** (max abs difference 4.5~36) and in the GDN `query`/`key`/`value`/`g`/`beta` inputs (0.4~6.8) on the very first step where both copies decode together. GDN state is therefore a downstream symptom, not the origin. Two consecutive steps with byte-identical GDN inputs still produce different outputs, which is explained by the already-diverged `state_before`, not by kernel nondeterminism.
- Because the layer-0 input already differs, the divergence must originate in the input token IDs, position IDs, or the MTP draft selection before layer 0. The GDN `actual_seq_lengths` pattern is also mixed-batch: batch=1 gives `indices=2 / seq_lens=2 / accept=1`, batch=2 gives `indices=4 / seq_lens=3 / accept=2`, with a zero-length segment in `seq_lens`.
- Request-level tracing explains part of that difference: the two identical prompts are not synchronized. One copy finishes prefill earlier and runs 1–2 positions ahead (`positions 11,12` for one copy vs `9,10` for the other), so the batch is a prefill+decode mix (`enable_chunked_prefill=True`). Any same-timestep logprob delta therefore mixes a real position-progress difference with numerical error and must not be read as a pure computation error. What remains valid is the final token-sequence divergence: two identical requests still produce different tokens from index 13 onward. This points at mixed-batch (prefill + decode) state handling rather than at a single forward-pass numerical bug.

## Reproduction

Use `qwen36_offline_parity.py` with the pinned model revision and:

```bash
QWEN36_OFFLINE_SPEC_TOKENS=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=2 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_MAX_TOKENS=24 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_ENFORCE_EAGER=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_GREEDY_ONLY=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_RESULT=qwen36-clean-repeat-a.json \
python3 -m pytest -sv qwen36_offline_parity.py
```

Repeat with result `qwen36-clean-repeat-b.json`, then compare the same runner across the two result files. - `qwen-recurrent-replay-v17.json` — recurrent replay determinism (see the cosine/max_abs_diff inconsistency above)

issue.title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B batched MTP is not batch-invariant: identical prompts in one batch diverge (MRV1 and MRV2)
issue.body:
## Summary

On Atlas 800T A3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8 with `qwen3_5_mtp` and two concurrent prompts is not reproducible within either MRV1 or MRV2. Both runners exceed the decode tolerance on the second prompt and both eventually diverge on token identity; on the first prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta stays within tolerance on both runners. With a single sequence in the batch the same prompt passes at 1.21e-06 and is byte-identical across cold starts. With two identical prompts in one batch, each runner produces two different final token sequences from index 13 onward, so the batch itself is not self-consistent for either runner. A single MRV1 run is therefore not a stable correctness baseline for batched MRV2, while the MRV2 kernel path itself shows no numerical regression.

This should be tracked as a shared batched speculative-decoding issue, not as evidence that an isolated MRV2 kernel is solely responsible.

## Environment

- vLLM / vLLM-Ascend: 0.30.0, with the local Qwen compatibility adaptation `qwen-v030@6b7590693ce8`
- Model revision: `1a118d717bcbd59480f4a110fe22181d21711b4d`
- CANN 9.2.1; torch 2.10.0; torch-npu 2.10.0.post7
- TP=1, FP16, W8A8, `qwen3_5_mtp`, one speculative token, seed 1234
- Two prompts, 24 output tokens, eager mode; graph+MTP also fails separately

## Expected behavior

Repeated cold starts of the same runner should satisfy the repository logprob comparison rules: prefill atol 0.0689 and decode atol 0.1378. Note that the harness applies the prefill tolerance only to the first generated token's logprob, so this is a narrow prefill check rather than a full prefill comparison. MRV1/MRV2 should then be compared under the same rules.

## Actual behavior

- Serial offline generation and batched generation without MTP pass the MRV1/MRV2 comparison.
- Batched MTP fails across MRV1/MRV2 in eager and graph modes.
- Single-sequence control: running the second prompt alone (`QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_OFFSET=1`, batch=1, MTP=1, eager, 24 tokens) passes. Two independent cold starts produce byte-identical JSON (both md5 `5deaa85f8e28c86ab8a4c22369df3546`), MRV1 and MRV2 token IDs are identical, and the maximum logprob delta is 1.21e-06; the within-runner delta is 0.0 for both runners. This localizes the defect to batched (batch>1) speculative decoding, not to the MRV2 kernel path.
- Identical-prompt batch control: submitting the same prompt twice in one batch (`QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_OFFSET=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_REPEAT=2`) fails within each runner. The two final token sequences are identical up to index 12 and diverge at index 13 (one copy emits `100606`, the other continues with `113895`). Since the inputs are identical, the divergence can only come from per-batch state, not from prompt content or accept-count heterogeneity. A heterogeneous two-prompt batch reproduces the same failure.
- Time-step trace shows the two requests are not synchronized: one copy finishes prefill earlier and runs 1–2 positions ahead, so the batch mixes prefill and decode. Logprob deltas taken from same-timestep snapshots are therefore contaminated by the position skew and are not usable as an error metric; the final-sequence divergence at index 13 is the valid observation.
- The cross-runner comparison operates on final token sequences and therefore remains valid; it reports 0.1676 in the homogeneous batch and 0.3020 in the heterogeneous batch. It is, however, not sensitive to the batch-level divergence, so the primary probe is the final token sequence of two identical requests in one batch.
- Independent no-probe cold starts also fail within each runner:
  - MRV1 A/B: the first prompt diverges at token 14; before that divergence the same-token logprob delta is at most 0.0386, i.e. within tolerance. The second prompt keeps identical token IDs but has four same-token logprob points above tolerance, up to 0.2473 (1.8x atol).
  - MRV2 A/B: prompts diverge at tokens 18 and 22. On the first prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta is 0.1294 (within tolerance); on the second prompt it is up to 0.3880 (2.8x atol) before divergence.
  - The "fails on both runners" claim is therefore driven by the second prompt; the first prompt stays within tolerance until its first token divergence.
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` was explicitly enabled in both engine logs, but the cross-runner comparison still fails. On the second prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta reaches 0.6634 (4.8x atol), so batch invariance alone does not restore agreement.
- Disabling shared-expert overlap is not a workaround: the second prompt still exceeds tolerance, and its divergence-point cross-lookup delta grows to 3.1767 (vs 1.7524 in the clean baseline). That 3.1767 is a cross-distribution value at the divergence point and is not comparable to the 0.6634 pre-divergence same-token value; under the pre-divergence same-token view the no-overlap delta is actually lower (0.2370). The conclusion is "not a fix", not "makes it worse".

## Isolation evidence

- Actual scheduled draft token IDs and positions are identical for the first ten GDN steps; the first scheduling mismatch appears later.
- Prefill metadata, cache indices, state dtype (`float32`), state stride, sequence lengths and scale match.
- With the original cache index layout preserved, the FP32-state fused recurrent implementation is bitwise-identical to itself across eight replays for each runner (`to_previous.max_abs_diff = 0.0`). Its comparison against the recorded output reports `max_abs_diff = 0.0` together with `cosine = 0.99991`, which is internally inconsistent; exact reproduction of the recorded output is therefore not established. These data support determinism under a fixed input, not engine-level reproducibility or the absence of recurrent-operator sensitivity.
- Disabling MTP makes the batched comparison pass in our local control runs, and eager+MTP fails, so the issue is not limited to graph replay. The no-MTP control file is not yet attached to this report.
- The batch=1 control above passes at 1.21e-06 with two byte-identical cold starts, so the Qwen3.6 MRV2 adaptation does not introduce a numerical regression by itself; the failure requires more than one sequence in the batch.
- Because identical prompts in one batch already diverge, the defect is a batch-level self-consistency problem shared by MRV1 and MRV2, not a runner-to-runner numerical difference. This also explains why `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` did not help: that switch addresses reduction order, while the observed divergence is consistent with per-sequence state or cache-index handling.
- `enable_prefix_caching` is ruled out: rerunning the identical-prompt batch with prefix caching disabled still produces two different final token sequences, with the first divergence moving to tokens 10/19 instead of token 13. The batch-level divergence is therefore not caused by shared prefix blocks.
- The original `recurrent_gated_delta_rule` cannot be used as a kernel-side control: with fp32 state it fails inside `fla_npu` at `aclnnRecurrentGatedDeltaRuleGetWorkspaceSize` with error `161002`, which is why the adaptation routes fp32 state to `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule`. A kernel-side A/B has to be done by state tracing rather than by reverting the path.
- State tracing moves the root cause earlier than GDN. In the identical-prompt batch, the two copies already differ in the **layer-0 input hidden states** (max abs difference 4.5~36) and in the GDN `query`/`key`/`value`/`g`/`beta` inputs (0.4~6.8) on the very first step where both copies decode together. GDN state is therefore a downstream symptom, not the origin. Two consecutive steps with byte-identical GDN inputs still produce different outputs, which is explained by the already-diverged `state_before`, not by kernel nondeterminism.
- Because the layer-0 input already differs, the divergence must originate in the input token IDs, position IDs, or the MTP draft selection before layer 0. The GDN `actual_seq_lengths` pattern is also mixed-batch: batch=1 gives `indices=2 / seq_lens=2 / accept=1`, batch=2 gives `indices=4 / seq_lens=3 / accept=2`, with a zero-length segment in `seq_lens`.
- Request-level tracing explains part of that difference: the two identical prompts are not synchronized. One copy finishes prefill earlier and runs 1–2 positions ahead (`positions 11,12` for one copy vs `9,10` for the other), so the batch is a prefill+decode mix (`enable_chunked_prefill=True`). Any same-timestep logprob delta therefore mixes a real position-progress difference with numerical error and must not be read as a pure computation error. What remains valid is the final token-sequence divergence: two identical requests still produce different tokens from index 13 onward. This points at mixed-batch (prefill + decode) state handling rather than at a single forward-pass numerical bug.

## Reproduction

Use `qwen36_offline_parity.py` with the pinned model revision and:

```bash
QWEN36_OFFLINE_SPEC_TOKENS=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=2 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_MAX_TOKENS=24 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_ENFORCE_EAGER=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_GREEDY_ONLY=1 \
QWEN36_OFFLINE_RESULT=qwen36-clean-repeat-a.json \
python3 -m pytest -sv qwen36_offline_parity.py
```

Repeat with result `qwen36-clean-repeat-b.json`, then compare the same runner across the two result files. For the single-sequence control use the same command with `QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_COUNT=1 QWEN36_OFFLINE_PROMPT_OFFSET=1` and a different result path; the offset selects the second prompt, which is the one that fails in the batched case. The greedy-only flag is used only to reduce diagnostic runtime; it is not a substitute for the full accuracy matrix. Two side effects must be noted: (a) with this flag the harness short-circuits `mrv1_sampled_reproducible`, `mrv2_sampled_reproducible`, `mrv1_sampled_repo_tolerance_pass` and `mrv2_sampled_repo_tolerance_pass` to `true` even though no sampled outputs were collected, so those four fields are not evidence; (b) the test is expected to fail at the `assert greedy_repo_tolerance_pass` line, after the JSON result has already been written.

For the batch-invariant control, add `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. The engine log must contain `Enabling batch-invariant mode for vLLM on Ascend NPU.`

## Evidence files

- `qwen36-repeatability-summary.json` — comparison index and interpretation. Its `within_runner_repeatability` max-delta field mixes post-divergence cross-lookups and does not reproduce from the raw files; use `qwen36-clean-repeat-a.json`/`b.json` directly for per-token deltas.
- `qwen36-clean-repeat-a.json`, `qwen36-clean-repeat-b.json` — no-probe cold-start raw outputs
- `qwen-token-only24-v20-comparison.json` — actual scheduled draft IDs and positions
- `qwen-recurrent-replay-v17.json` — recurrent replay determinism (see the cosine/max_abs_diff inconsistency above)
- `qwen-gdn0-meta-worker-state0-v19.json` — prefill metadata, state layout and numerical comparisons
- `qwen36-batch-invariant-eager24.json` — batch-invariant control
- `qwen36-no-overlap-eager24.json` — shared-expert overlap ablation
- `qwen36-p1-b1-a.json`, `qwen36-p1-b1-b.json` — batch=1 single-prompt control, two cold starts, identical md5
- `qwen36-mix-homo.json` — batch=2 with the same prompt twice; same-runner self-divergence at token 13
- `qwen36-mix-hetero.json` — batch=2 with two different prompts, same-session reproduction of the failure
- `qwen36-nopc-homo.json` — identical-prompt batch with `enable_prefix_caching=False`; still self-diverges

## Requested investigation

With batch=1 the two runners agree to 1.21e-06 and are bitwise reproducible across cold starts; with two identical prompts in one batch, the scheduler runs one copy 1–2 positions ahead, so prefill and decode are mixed in the same batch (`enable_chunked_prefill=True`, zero-length segment in `actual_seq_lengths`), and the two copies end with different tokens from index 13 onward. The mixed prefill+decode batch is therefore structural for Qwen3.5 GDN, not an optional switch; the state update has to be checked under this required configuration.

issue.title: [Feature][AuxOutput] Replay ordinary raw indexer selections
issue.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Return ordinary sparse-attention TopK selections through the existing AuxOutput
SHM lifecycle. This is the raw-int32 foundation for #47280; Profile/Codec model
formats are separated into #62915 and host-memory admission into #63535.

## Claims

- Capture ordinary raw selections from DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5.2, the shared MLA
  path and Dots3 NOTE. Preserve actual source-layer order, TopK order and padding.
- Capture DeepSeek V4 C4A's raw compressed-cache indices without expanding token
  coordinates or adding a Profile; HCA/SWA layers add no source planes.
- Support Indexer-only and combined routed-expert output using existing accepted
  cursors, prefix restoration, async copying, SHM hashes and teardown.
- Allocate the persistent Indexer capture buffer through main's merged #63237
  profiling path, before the profiling forward and automatic KV sizing. Clone
  each step's active rows for asynchronous transfer.
- Return `indexer_topk` through Python output/APIs and Rust engine IPC plus the
  Rust token `/inference/v1/generate` path. Rust Indexer OpenAI delivery is not
  included. Raw layout is `[tokens, sources, topk]`, int32.

## Validation

Current scoped checks after merging main `5c8ae7c74a` (change `192f4fbd65`):

- Ruff lint/format hooks pass for the four changed Python files. Focused mypy
  (`--follow-imports=skip --ignore-missing-imports`) passes for the Connector,
  Indexer capturer and Indexer CPU suite; test-tethering checks pass for both
  touched suites.
- 27 source-isolated CPU cases pass: 23 existing helper, worker/storage,
  dual-pending-step and profiling cases, plus four Tensor snapshot checks
  covering empty/partial/full rows, storage independence and output-rank gating.
  Isolation avoids platform-dependent imports; these are not full model or
  full-suite runs.
- Normal pytest collection remains blocked by missing `uvloop` on Windows.
  Full pre-commit was blocked by its mypy environment build (Windows
  placeholder-wheel build, WinError 183); individual Ruff hooks pass.
  No new GPU/H20, KV-capacity, CUDA Graph, model-quality or Rust build validation
  is claimed.

```bash
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_indexer_capture.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py
```

The user's [pre-split verification report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49555#issuecomment-6383532867) applies to
`81d09a837` with full-size dummy-weight models. It is historical evidence for raw
replay and the now-separated admission cases, not validation of this merged
profiling lifecycle or real-weight model quality.

## Details

`GPUModelRunner.profile_run()` creates the Connector, whose constructor allocates
and binds each enabled capturer. Indexer's persistent device buffer therefore
enters automatic KV memory profiling outside the weights pool. Per-step snapshots
clone the active rows for asynchronous transfer. `snapshot()` returns the cloned Tensor
directly; the single-field `IndexerSnapshot` wrapper is removed. Real KV initialization reuses the Connector and calls
`initialize_output_storage()` with the resolved layout on the output TP rank.
Main's fallback remains when profiling was skipped; explicit KV byte budgets
remain manual. There is no separate GPUWorker load-model capture hook or
`initialize_capturers()` phase. Startup Plan schema follows main (version 2).

Capture remains immediately after actual logical TopK scoring and before an
attention backend can overwrite shared buffers. Explicit source capabilities,
non-contiguous layer-to-column mapping, MTP/shared-consumer exclusion and existing
forced-scoring/skip conditions remain. No Python forward hooks or validity bitmap
are introduced. The existing Indexer close/unbind and graph-before-buffer teardown
are retained. V4 backbone replay disables the unscored short-context shortcut;
MTP keeps its original shortcut. ROCm V4 monokernel bypasses the common capture
entry and is explicitly rejected with Indexer Replay. Duplicate persistent
Indexer allocation is removed. This update does not change R3 snapshot behavior.

Both artifacts share row-count/range extraction with independent prompt offsets.
Current-step output slices reuse the separately owned typed CPU arrays; packed
rows still feed SHM storage. History restoration uses common unpacking that keeps
combined artifacts contiguous and independent, and store-backed Indexer output
writable. NumPy views retain the CPU allocation until the consumer releases them.
Storage layout calculation returns the per-token shape and dtype separately from
SHM initialization. No latency improvement is claimed without measurement.
Generic SHM buffering/publication/materialization lives in `artifacts.py`; packed
record widths determine default KV-derived arena capacity. Host probing, admission
and its environment override/tests are reviewed separately in #63535, based on
main, so this PR can be reviewed independently of that policy.

MRV2 generate and prefix caching are required; existing PP/DCP/PCP, adaptive
verification and remote-PD restrictions remain. V4.1, GLM-5.3 KPool, Qwen QSA,
Step5 and HY-V4 Profile formats belong to #62915; MiniMax-M3 has no adapter.
See `docs/training/indexer_replay.md` for the output format and limits.

This updates the existing #49555 rather than creating a competing PR; #63237 is
reused from main, and the two split PRs cover distinct admission/model contracts.
AI assistance was used. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing
all changed lines and completing relevant validation before requesting review.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses main's profiling lifecycle and separates raw replay from admission/Profile policy.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Scoped checks pass; full pytest/pre-commit and current runtime/GPU validation remain outstanding as described above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Ruff passes; raw usage, allocation timing and support limits are documented.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Current scope, split boundaries, evidence and validation limits are recorded.
</details>

### Rust frontend verification on H20

**Commit:** `a9404cfe03` (branch head).
**Environment:** SGP H20e, `vllm-sgp-h20-05`, Slurm job 5151/5163, no container. Toolchain: host `rustc 1.95.0` + `cargo-nextest`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` on node-local NVMe.

The node image (Alibaba Cloud Linux 3, glibc 2.32) has no OpenSSL development headers, and the prebuilt Ubuntu 22.04 `openssl-ctr` cannot be linked there (`undefined reference: stat@GLIBC_2.33`). The workspace's `--all-features` build selects `vllm-cmd/native-tls-vendored`, so `openssl-src` builds OpenSSL from source; that path failed because the node's stripped `perl-base` is missing `IPC::Cmd`, `FindBin` and `Time::Piece`.

Fixed the environment with three checked-in perl stubs (`$HOME/vllm-shared/perl5-stub`, `PERL5LIB` exported): `IPC::Cmd` with `can_run()`, `FindBin` with an absolute `$FindBin::Bin`, and `Time::Piece` with `localtime`/`gmtime`/`strftime`/`strptime("%d %b %Y")`. Vendored OpenSSL then compiles against the node's own glibc — no container, no glibc mismatch. Note `-p <crate> --all-features` does **not** enable this feature (package-scoped), so the workspace must be selected.

Commands, matching `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`:

```console
$ cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
$ cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
$ cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

Results:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: **exit 0**, no diffs.
- `cargo clippy ... -D warnings`: **exit 0**.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`: **2455 tests run, 2455 passed, 13 skipped**, exit 0.
  - The first pass had one failure, `vllm-chat::roundtrip::roundtrip_gemma4`, a cold-cache HF tokenizer download; it passed when rerun alone and the full suite is green on the rerun.
- `uv` was on `PATH`, so `vllm-engine-core-client::python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` ran its Python fixture instead of failing to spawn it.

Not run: `cargo sort` / `cargo deny` (binaries unavailable on this image). Safe to omit here because the diff against `main` only touches `rust/**/*.rs` and `src/tests/python_compat.py`, not `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`. No live Rust HTTP server against a real engine was exercised; the route tests in `vllm-server` are included in the workspace run.
