issue.body:
## Overview

Use the unified PyTorch accelerator APIs for backend-independent operations in `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer`, following #30679 and existing vLLM usage.

## Claims

- Replace availability checks, device selection, synchronization, and current-stream lookups that do not pass streams to CUDA-specific communication APIs.
- Use `torch.Event` for sharded-RDT slot and quantization dependencies.
- Preserve stream-level synchronization boundaries, NCCL stream interfaces, and CUDA IPC behavior.

## Validation

Passed on Windows with PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu:

- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files <six changed files>`
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files <six changed files>`
- Direct runs of `tools/pre_commit/check_torch_cuda.py`, `check_spdx_header.py`, `check_init_lazy_imports.py`, and `check_forbidden_imports.py` on the changed files.
- Python AST syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

Attempted with `PYTHONUTF8=1`:

```text
uv run --no-sync -- .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_plan.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_producer.py -q
```

Pytest fails while loading the repository conftest because `uvloop` is unavailable in this Windows environment; no tests reached execution. Full pre-commit is blocked by cache permissions and a Git Bash `NtCreateDirectoryObject` failure with a fresh writable cache. The mypy hook could not initialize. Commits include DCO sign-off; the broken commit hooks were bypassed after running the available checks separately.

No GPU transfer test or model evaluation was performed on this CPU-only host. Human line-by-line review and hardware validation remain pending, so this PR is a draft. No output-quality, performance, or new-backend support claim is made.

## Details

### Evidence of existing unified API use in vLLM

These links point to upstream commit `7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a`:

| API / pattern | Existing upstream use |
| --- | --- |
| Availability check followed by device synchronization | [WorkerBase.synchronize_device](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py#L129-L133) uses `torch.accelerator.is_available()` and `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`. |
| Current-stream synchronization | [EPLB communicator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py#L227-L232) already uses `torch.accelerator.current_stream().synchronize()`. |
| Device selection in a background thread | [EPLB async worker](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py#L31-L34) uses `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device_index)`. |
| Device-index context manager | [PyNcclCommunicator initialization](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py#L175-L182) uses `torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index)`. |
| Generic events for cross-thread dependencies | [EPLB CpuGpuEvent](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_utils.py#L49-L59) constructs `torch.Event()`. |
| Current stream queried for an explicit tensor device | [Mooncake embedding backend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a64fb8fc9239cb65e0df9313fa759594dfb206a/vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/mooncake_store_embedding/backend.py#L209-L214) records a `torch.Event` on `torch.accelerator.current_stream(tensor.device)`. |

Earlier merged migrations include #36085 (synchronization), #36145 (device count/current device/device selection), and #36144 (device contexts). These establish existing API use; runtime validation of this patch remains pending as described above.

### Compatibility and scope

Generic streams do not expose the `.cuda_stream` field consumed by the current NCCL wrappers. Communication stream lookups and stream constructors/contexts are retained, including sharded-RDT contexts that update vLLM's cached current-stream tracking. Device UUID lookup and CUDA IPC collection also remain unchanged.

The earlier global event migration was reverted in #47668 because `torch.Event` ignored the `blocking` parameter ([upstream explanation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47081#issuecomment-4874967250)). This patch only replaces default, nonblocking events.

Duplicate-work checks covered #30679 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and `weight_transfer accelerator`. #57374 overlaps the NCCL post-send availability check and changes that stream lookup through vLLM's helper as part of a new transport. This patch additionally covers IPC, packed-buffer stream tracking, sparse NCCL synchronization, and sharded-RDT device/event handling. #57022, #33225, and #37134 address stream/platform or communicator migrations; their interfaces are retained here. This patch does not add a transport or change rendezvous behavior.

AI assistance was used to implement this change and prepare this description.

issue.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM is a framework support multi hardware backend. while there are some torch.cuda hard code call. this is unfriendly to non-cuda compatible device. Fortunately, there is a new set of `torch.accelerator` [API](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/accelerator.html) in pytorch which can dispatch based on platform.

Meanwhile, we should add some lint tools to avoid add more `torch.cuda` call in new added code. first example is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30681. 

### Proposed Change.

Target time: Migration done by end of Q2(or earlier). 

torch accelerator API status on torch-2.9.0:

|cuda API name| unified torch API name| torch API Status | vLLM replace status| 
|-------|-------|-------|-------|
|[torch.cuda.Event](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cuda.Event.html)| [torch.Event](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Event.html) | torch 2.9 ready| ~done #26985~  #47140|
|[torch.cuda.Stream](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cuda.Stream.html)| [torch.Stream](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Stream.html) | ~torch 2.9 ready~  2.11 (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/171040)| https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37134|

Opened #63457 as a focused follow-up to this RFC for weight-transfer availability, device selection, synchronization, and default events. The PR description includes pinned upstream code links showing the same APIs already used by WorkerBase, EPLB, PyNcclCommunicator, and Mooncake.

Scope difference from the existing open work: #57374 overlaps the NCCL post-send availability check and stream lookup as part of adding a torch.distributed transport. #63457 also covers IPC, packed-buffer stream tracking, sparse NCCL synchronization, and sharded-RDT device/event handling, while retaining the current communication stream interfaces and transport selection. The stream/context migrations in #57022, #33225, and #37134 remain separate. The PR is a draft with its validation gaps documented.

issue.title: [RFC]: RL Roadmap Q4 2026
issue.body:
### Motivation.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is now a first-class workload for vLLM Ascend. Frameworks such as verl, slime, and vime keep a rollout engine alive for an entire training job and drive it through a lifecycle that ordinary serving never exercises:

- `sleep(level)` / `wake_up(tags)` to hand NPU memory back to a colocated trainer, then take it back;
- `pause_generation(mode)` / `resume_generation()` to stop scheduling while weights change;
- `init_weight_transfer_engine` / `start_weight_update` / `update_weights` / `finish_weight_update` to reload weights in place over HCCL or NPU IPC;
- routed-expert capture (`--enable-return-routed-experts`) and replay so that the trainer reuses the routing decisions produced by inference;
- batch-invariant execution and reproducible logprobs so that training and inference agree.

Every one of these paths is cross-cutting: it touches the worker, the model runner, the memory allocator, ACL graph capture, HCCL, the KV connectors, and every model, quantization, and attention implementation. That is why the same class of defect keeps reappearing. A tensor is silently discarded by sleep. A derived weight is not refreshed after reload. An ACL graph replays with storage that was replaced. A test passes because it only asserts that the API returned successfully.

During Q3 the community wrote three open RFCs that describe the contracts we need:

- **#16558** - Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend.
- **#16322** - Make live weight updates transactional and graph-safe.
- **#12073** - RL test case upgrade.

Those RFCs are the technical core of this roadmap. This issue is the Q4 2026 delivery plan that connects them, adds the replay and code-refactoring workstreams, and lists the RFCs and pull requests that are already in flight so that contributors can see where each item stands and what is still missing.

The roadmap exists because the work is larger than any single PR series, because several items block each other (an allocation boundary must land before owner hooks can be validated; capture layouts must land before topology tests are meaningful), and because we want reviewers to be able to judge each PR against a stated contract instead of against the absence of an immediate failure.

#### Scope of Q4 2026

Five workstreams:

1. **Sleep mode correctness** - tensor ownership and recovery across sleep/wake, including extra cleanup and ACL graph.
2. **Live weight update correctness** - one transactional reload contract for HCCL, NPU IPC, and future backends.
3. **RL test case upgrade** - lifecycle-oriented tests that fail when behavior is wrong, not when an API is merely reachable.
4. **Replay feature enhancement** - Router Replay (R3) capture/replay correctness across topologies and scheduling modes, plus related consistency features.
5. **RL code refactoring** - Worker interface refactor, HCCL weight-update inheritance from the upstream engine, and CaMemAllocator inheritance from the upstream allocator.

#### Status snapshot at filing

| # | Workstream | Tracking RFC | Design state | Q4 outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Sleep mode | #16558 | Ownership contract proposed; phased migration in the RFC | No persistent non-KV tensor is discarded silently by either level, and every releasable buffer is released or documented with a measured size |
| 2 | Weight update | #16322 | Transaction contract proposed; Phase 0 largely landed | HCCL and IPC execute one transaction; derived state is graph-stable |
| 3 | RL tests | #12073 | Test tree designed; partial implementation | PR-gating lifecycle subset plus a nightly matrix |
| 4 | Replay | this issue (no dedicated RFC yet) | Upstream capture-layout contract in review | Topology-complete R3 capture/replay; indexer replay scoped upstream |
| 5 | Refactoring | #18920 (Worker), this issue (transfer, allocator) | Scoped; first pieces merged | Thin adapters over the upstream Worker, NCCL engine, and CuMem allocator |

The RFC/PR lists below were collected from GitHub at filing time and will drift. The tracking RFC remains the source of truth for design detail; this issue tracks delivery.

#### Principles

1. **Upstream first.** Extend the upstream vLLM contract or contribute a hook upstream before adding another Ascend-specific exception. Inherit orchestration; own device mechanisms.
2. **One contract per lifecycle.** Sleep/wake owns memory reclamation. Weight update owns representation. Capture owns logical expert IDs. A feature may not repair a failure that belongs to another lifecycle.
3. **Fail closed.** If a post-capture representation change cannot preserve the storage an ACL graph captured, raise an actionable error instead of silently replacing it.
4. **Tests must be able to fail.** Assert physical memory, `data_ptr()` stability, and output/logprob equality against a fresh cold load. A test that only checks a return code is not coverage.
5. **Measure, do not assume.** Reclaimed memory, wake latency, update throughput, and capture overhead are reported in the PR that changes them.

#### Non-goals

- New RL algorithms, trainer-side changes, or wire-protocol redesign.
- Guaranteeing arbitrary structural model changes during a live update.
- Preserving active-request KV contents across sleep.
- Automatic level-2 parameter reload; the caller-driven reload/update sequence is unchanged.
- Feature parity for Model Runner V1 beyond keeping it startable while it is deprecated (#18202).

---

### Proposed Change.

Each workstream below states the problem, the Q4 deliverables, the existing RFCs and PRs, and the exit criteria. Deliverables are checkboxes so that progress is visible in the issue; a box may only be checked when the change is merged and the stated test exists.

#### 1. Sleep mode correctness

**Problem.** `CaMemAllocator` tags an allocation according to the active pool. `Worker.initialize_from_config()` enters `use_memory_pool(tag="kv_cache")` around the entire `model_runner.initialize_kv_cache()` call, so attention-backend metadata, input-batch state, speculative state, connector registration, sparse-KV/KVPP runtime state, and graph metadata are all created in a discardable scope. At level 1 those allocations are released; at level 2 they are discarded together with the weights. On wake, storage is recreated at the same virtual address, so pointers stay valid while contents do not. An ACL graph can therefore replay with a valid pointer to an erased scale, sentinel, or device pointer table, which surfaces as accuracy loss, a wrong routing decision, or a hang.

**Q4 deliverables.**

Failure visibility (P0)

- [ ] Land the deterministic remap-poison helper: in a fresh subprocess, wrap the NPU remap operation and fill every newly mapped allocation with a recognizable nonzero pattern before the normal host backup is restored.
- [ ] Allocator contract test: allocate a host-backed weight, a KV tensor, and unrelated metadata in a `kv_cache` scope; assert stable addresses, restored weights, and lost KV/metadata contents.
- [ ] Level-2 ownership classification test: parameter, non-persistent registered buffer, and plain tensor attribute; after a poisoned wake and a simulated reload only the first two may recover.
- [ ] One ACL-graph reproducer that captures a graph using a nonzero persistent scale created in the KV scope and fails under the current broad scope.
- [ ] Publish the tensor-ownership inventory (owner, allocation tag, recovery class, first post-wake reader, graph-capture status, test coverage) for MRV1, MRV2, and 310P. The inventory is the acceptance checklist for the migration.

Allocation boundary (P1)

- [ ] Split KV initialization into preparation, cache allocation, and binding; only raw cache backing and its shaped views stay inside `use_memory_pool(tag="kv_cache")`.
- [ ] Apply the same boundary to MRV2, and evaluate 310P independently while preserving its unsupported-feature guards.
- [ ] Move attention-backend metadata, input-batch bookkeeping, speculative/state-space state, connector objects and registration metadata, KVPP runtime state, and graph-manager metadata into the binding phase.
- [ ] Add an allocation audit asserting that only cache backing is tagged `kv_cache` in representative configurations.

Owner recovery protocol (P1)

- [ ] Define a runner-owned lifecycle protocol (`post_sleep_wake(discarded_tags)` / `post_weights_reload()`) with an explicit owner registry; do not traverse arbitrary Python objects to discover tensors.
- [ ] Enforce recovery order: allocator mappings and host-backed bytes, registered model buffers, level-2 reload, derived weights, runtime/HCCL/synchronization state, ACL graph recapture, then admit scheduling.
- [ ] Fold the existing `post_kv_cache_wake_up()` compatibility behavior into this lifecycle as upstream compatibility allows.
- [ ] Convert confirmed static tensors to registered non-persistent buffers or host values; document every remaining `sleep_persistent` allocation with owner, size, and rationale.

Extra cleanup and graphs (P1)

- [ ] Require every owner whose resources extra cleanup destroys to declare graph invalidation; recapture before admitting new work.
- [ ] Verify that re-created HCCL metadata and device pointer arrays reference post-wake resources.
- [ ] Run every touched backend path through at least two sleep/wake cycles, not one.

Model-specific sleep regressions (P1, continuous)

- [ ] DeepSeek-V4.1 sleep defects (#18491), RoPE and derived cos/sin caches (#17217, #18986), MoE layout and L2 communication state (#12269, #12651), target/draft-private state (#18624), and KV-pool interaction (#18118) are fixed or explicitly deferred with a tracking issue.

Reclamation completeness (P0, transactional)

**Problem.** Sleep currently releases two CaMem pools and - only when `rl_config.sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` is enabled - the ACL graphs and the HCCL process groups. Everything else the engine allocates stays in the default torch_npu pool, which sleep never touches: on Ascend there is no `workspace`, `runtime` or `cudagraph` pool, no owner registry, and no per-owner release hook. Upstream closed the same gap on GPU in vllm-project/vllm#59055 by tagging each owner (`workspace` vllm-project/vllm#59156, `runtime` vllm-project/vllm#59158, `cudagraph` vllm-project/vllm#59160, DeepEP vllm-project/vllm#59939, allreduce workspace vllm-project/vllm#59360). This deliverable is the Ascend equivalent, and it is a transaction: accounting first, then tags, then release/restore, then verification, with no step skipped and every number measured.

**Measured baseline** (Ascend 910B 64 GiB die, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.14`, one die, vLLM Ascend `b173effde`, torch_npu 2.10.0, CANN 9.1.0, 2026-10-24). "Mine" is device HBM in use minus the pre-initialisation baseline of the same process, so a neighbour's allocations on the die cancel out.

| Configuration | Awake | Level-1 asleep | Freed | Residual | Sleep | Wake |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `--enforce-eager` | 9.277 | 0.529 | 8.748 | **0.529** | 2.31 s | 0.32 s |
| ACL graph (default) | 9.473 | 0.725 | 8.748 | **0.725** | 2.43 s | 0.31 s |
| ACL graph + `sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` | 9.582 | 0.457 | 9.125 | **0.457** | 2.40 s (level 2: 3.54 s) | 4.01 s (level 2: 7.39 s) |

Values in GiB except the latency columns. The ACL-graph residual decomposes as 419.2 MiB of inactive blocks stranded in the `weights` pool, 292.0 MiB of ACL graph memory pool, 24.0 MiB of live default-pool tensors and <= 15 MiB of CANN runtime and stream state; that accounts for 99% of the measured residual. Extra cleanup buys 0.268 GiB (the graph pool and the captured graph workspaces) for a 13x wake-up cost. On this model the largest single releasable item is not a graph at all: it is the weights pool waste, which no configuration releases.

**What stays resident while asleep, and whether it can be released.**

| Resident while asleep | Where it comes from | Measured | Releasable | How |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Inactive blocks inside the `weights` CaMem pool | `CaMemAllocator` cannot `empty_cache` a pluggable pool (`device_allocator/camem.py`, the `TODO` in `use_memory_pool`) | 419.2 MiB of 1586 MiB (26%) | Yes | trim or compact the pool before the CPU backup, or allocate weight-repacking temporaries in a separate discardable pool |
| ACL graph memory pool | `Platform._global_graph_pool`, `ACLGraphWrapper.graph_pool` (`compilation/acl_graph.py:117`) | 292.0 MiB reserved, 0 active | Yes | drop the handle on sleep and recapture on wake; today only extra cleanup releases it, and it never drops the platform handle |
| Recorded graph op workspaces (`capture_resources`, e.g. `npu_fused_infer_attention_score.workspace`) and `_graph_params.workspaces` | `compilation/acl_graph.py`, `compilation/updatable_graph.py` | 1.43 GiB of references over 150 entries; 274 MiB actually returned | Yes | already cleared by `AclGraphSleepWakeupManager.sleep()`; report it and release the pool behind it |
| HCCL process groups (7 at TP=1) | `HcclSleepWakeupManager` | ~0 MiB returned to the driver at TP=1 | Partly | destroy/restore exists; must be measured at TP8/EP8, where the equivalent NCCL buffers are 1.26-1.64 GiB/GPU upstream |
| Attention and context-parallel scratch sized by tokens x hidden | `attention/dsa_v1.py:1691-1719` (`_oproj_send_buf`, `_oproj_recv_buf`, `_oproj_rs_out_buf`), `attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py:648` and `:921`, `attention/context_parallel/dsa_cp.py:2244`, `attention/dsa_v41.py:601-605` | not allocated on the 0.6B dense path | Yes | `workspace` pool |
| MoE dispatch and combine buffers, expert counters, EPLB tables | `ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py:276`, `ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py`, `ops/fused_moe/eplb.py` | not measured yet (needs a MoE reference configuration) | Yes for scratch, no for state | split `workspace` and `runtime` |
| Speculative-decoding draft state (MTP/EAGLE/DFlash) | `worker/v2/spec_decode/*` | not measured yet | Yes | `runtime` pool |
| Weight-transfer packed buffers | `distributed/weight_transfer/packed_tensor.py` (`DEFAULT_PACKED_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES = 1 GiB`, `DEFAULT_PACKED_NUM_BUFFERS = 2`) | 2 GiB HCCL or 1 GiB NPU IPC per rank while a transfer is in flight | Yes | free them at `finish_weight_update`, or tag them `workspace` |
| Sparse-KV offload and KVPP runtime arenas | `distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/.../sparse_kv_offload_manager.py` | feature dependent | Yes | owner hook |
| `sleep_persistent` tag (DSA Hadamard, ...) | `device_allocator/camem.py` | small, by design | No | document the size and rationale per allocation |
| CANN runtime, streams, kernel modules | driver | <= 15 MiB once the weights-pool waste is excluded | No | - |

**The transaction.**

- [ ] T0 - Accounting before anything else: a `sleep_memory_report()` worker RPC that reports, at every stage, device free/used, per-tag CaMem bytes, per-pool reserved/active/inactive, the graph-pool reservation, the HCCL communicator count, and the delta attributed to the last release step. Today `SleepWakeupManager.sleep()` logs "released HCCL and attention workspace memory: 0.000 GiB" in every measured run, because it samples free memory around its own calls, before the allocator releases the cache; nothing below is "done" without a number from T0.
- [ ] T1 - Tags: add `workspace`, `runtime` and `cudagraph` pools matching vllm-project/vllm#59156, #59158 and #59160, and move the owners in the table above into them, one owner per PR.
- [ ] T2 - Release and restore: give every tagged owner an explicit discard-versus-backup policy and a restore path; keep `sleep_persistent` only for state that cannot be rebuilt.
- [ ] T3 - Verification per phase: bit-exact wake, ten sleep/wake cycles with a flat device-memory slope, a stated host RAM budget for the CPU backup, and sleep/wake latency before and after.
- [ ] T4 - Fail closed: if a live ACL graph references storage that a release step discarded, raise instead of replaying stale storage, and record the invalidation in the owner registry.

**Exit criteria for the transaction.**

- Every row of the resident table is either released or documented non-releasable with a measured size.
- Residual asleep memory is reported for the dense one-card reference above, a TP8/EP8 MoE reference, and a two-card configuration, and is non-increasing after each phase.
- Wake-up latency for the default (no extra cleanup) path does not regress by more than 2x.
- A PR-gating test fails when a new allocation site lands outside a tagged pool.

**Existing RFCs and PRs.**

- #16558 - `[RFC] Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend` (open). Upstream counterpart: vllm-project/vllm#53343.
- vllm-project/vllm#59055 - `[RFC]: Release all releasable GPU memory in sleep mode` (upstream tracking issue; its per-owner release PRs - #59156 workspace, #59158 runtime, #59160 cudagraph, #59939 DeepEP, #59360 allreduce workspace - are what this deliverable mirrors on Ascend).
- #18838 - `[bugfix] preserve configured parameters across level-2 sleep on Ascend` (merged).
- #16725 - `[BugFix][Sleep Mode] Register level-2 runtime tensors as non-persistent buffers` (merged).
- #13352 - `[BugFix] Restore MoE and DSA control buffers after level-2 wake` (merged).
- #13757 - `[BugFix][Device Allocator] Fix CaMem sleep race with in-flight graph replay` (merged).
- #15340 - `[BugFix][Sleep] Keep a dedicated 1 MiB HCCL lifecycle anchor` (merged).
- #13005 - `[MRV2][Feature] Support sleep-mode` (merged).
- #17666 / #18338 - `Synchronize NPU worker device` in sleep/wake (merged; the second is the v0.30.0 backport).
- #10775 - isolate KV cache from sleep cleanup with a dedicated tag for the Hadamard matrix (merged; see #17025).
- #15702 - `Fix CaMem sleep race with in-flight graph replay` (open follow-up to #13757).
- #12651 - refresh Ascend MoE communication state after L2 wake (open).
- #12269 - `[BugFix][Worker] Fix MoE sleep wakeup layout` (open).
- #17217 - RoPE does not recover after L2 wake (open).
- #18491 - fix sleep mode bug of DeepSeek-V4.1 (open).
- #18624 - preserve selected target and draft-private state across L2 sleep (open).
- #18986 - materialise contiguous RoPE derived cos/sin caches (open; references #16558).

#### 2. Live weight update correctness

**Problem.** `process_weights_after_loading()` currently performs checkpoint-to-runtime layout conversion, quantization repacking, derived-weight construction, backend buffer preparation, and memory disposal. A cold-load finalizer is therefore reused as a hot-reload mechanism, although many implementations are not idempotent and allocate new storage. Three invariants are missing:

1. **Representation correctness before load** - every destination is restored to the representation its weight loader expects.
2. **Value freshness after load** - every derived or runtime-only tensor is refreshed from the new source weights in dependency order.
3. **Storage identity before graph replay** - graph-visible persistent tensors and backend bindings still reference the storage ACLGraph captured.

Observed failure patterns include reassignment after `.to()`, `.contiguous()`, `.clone()`, or `npu_format_cast()`; checkpoint/runtime layout mismatch on the next reload; stale `weight_fp32`, `W_UK_T`/`W_UV`, composed projections, scales, and biases; destructive source disposal; non-idempotent work tied to `wake_up()` even though asynchronous RL may never sleep; runtime-owned plain tensors and expert lists that generic layerwise reload cannot see; and different semantics between HCCL and NPU IPC.

**Q4 deliverables.**

Transaction parity (P0)

- [ ] Every backend (HCCL, NPU IPC, future) executes START, LOAD, FINISH with identical semantics, and `model.load_weights(weights)` is called exactly once per chunk on both packed and unpacked paths.
- [ ] Unit tests assert call order, packed/unpacked equivalence, and cleanup when a step raises.
- [ ] No production path repairs checkpoint representation through `wake_up()`.

- [ ] Migrate the remaining derived state onto it: 310P `weight_nz`, composed model-specific projections, scales and scale biases, MoE/EPLB expert lists, workspaces, and offloader/kernel aliases.
- [ ] Add `data_ptr()` and storage-identity tests across at least three reloads after graph capture.

- [ ] Integrate MXFP8 and block-FP8 restore-before-load behavior into the common transaction.

#### 4. Replay feature enhancement

**Problem.** Router Replay (R3) is what makes MoE RL correct: the trainer replays the expert selections made during inference so that the gradient does not mix different routing decisions for the same tokens. On Ascend the capture path has been carried by a monkey patch, and it has repeatedly produced wrong logical IDs when the physical rows are not simply the tensor shape: TP-local shards, DP-gathered rows, MC2/SP padded shards, hybrid attention, and `AsyncLLM` scheduling all change the row layout or the timing. Replay also interacts with the two other workstreams: weights change between capture and replay, and sleep can discard the buffers that held the capture.

Q4 is therefore about replacing ad-hoc capture with an explicit layout contract, covering the topologies we support, and deciding the scope of indexer replay rather than shipping it half-designed.

Capture layout contract (P0)

- [ ] Adopt the upstream explicit row-layout API for routed-expert capture (vllm-project/vllm#61539, implementation PR vllm-project/vllm#62441) and pass shard sizes, gather groups, and ordered source ranges from the ALLGATHER, ALLTOALL, and MC2/FUSED_MC2 prepare paths.
- [ ] Capture logical expert IDs before expert remapping; keep the legacy router signature when capture is disabled.
- [ ] Delete `patch_routed_experts_capture.py` and its registration, and replace patch-specific tests with layout regression tests (#19561).
- [ ] Report an actionable error, rather than silent wrong output, when capture is requested without the required upstream API or in a rejected PCP/DCP/PP combination.

The RL paths accumulated their own copies of upstream flows. Three refactors remove most of that duplication and are prerequisites for the contracts above surviving the next upstream upgrade.

##### 5.1 Worker interface refactor

**Problem.** `NPUWorker` inherits `WorkerBase` and re-implements much of the upstream GPU Worker: `update_config`, `reload_weights`, weight-update orchestration, `execute_model` pipeline-parallel return handling, KV-cache setup, and lifecycle methods. #### Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream API drift (capture layouts, transfer engine, allocator) | Blocks a milestone; forces rework | Track the upstream PRs in this issue; land adapters behind capability checks; fail closed with an actionable message |
| ACL graph recapture cost | Wake or update latency regression | Recapture only when storage changed; measure both paths; keep in-place recovery the default |
| Refactor churn colliding with model bring-up | Merge conflicts, regressions | Stage by interface group; land inheritance behind contract tests; avoid touching unrelated model code |
| Test flakiness on NPU CI | Loss of trust in the matrix | Deterministic poisoning, fixed seeds, quarantine with an owner; no unbounded retries |
| Allocator change affecting serving memory accounting | Under- or over-reclaim in production | Keep serving tests green; report memory metrics in every allocator PR |
| Scope creep (sparse updates, LoRA, indexer replay) | Q4 objectives slip | These are P1/P2; they enter only when the P0 contracts are merged and tested |

#### Alternatives considered

**Continue with per-bug fixes.** Cheaper per fix, but the same defect classes reappear because there is no allocation boundary and no transaction. The Q3 fix list already shows repeated repairs of the same invariants.

**Always recapture ACL graphs after wake or update.** Avoids stale-state failures, but adds latency to every cycle and does not restore eager-mode state. Recapture is the fallback only when in-place recovery is impossible.

**Keep the routed-expert capture monkey patch.** It works for the simplest topology and fails whenever the physical row layout differs from the tensor shape; it also cannot express gather groups. The upstream explicit-layout API is the durable contract.

**Fork the upstream Worker flows.** Keeps Ascend behavior explicit, but every upstream fix must be ported by hand. Inheritance with narrow hooks is the cheaper long-term path, provided the override list is small and reviewed.

### Measurement evidence for the reclamation item (2026-10-24)

Measuring asleep memory instead of assuming it. **Method:** one LLM in one process on one Ascend 910B die (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.14`, vLLM Ascend `b173effde`, torch_npu 2.10.0, CANN 9.1.0). At every stage the probe records device free/used, per-tag CaMem bytes, per-pool reserved/active/inactive from `torch.npu.memory_snapshot()`, the ACL-graph inventory (wrappers, entries, recorded `capture_resources`) and the HCCL group count. "Mine" subtracts the pre-initialisation baseline of the same process, so a neighbour's allocation on the die cancels out.

| Configuration | Awake | Level-1 asleep | Freed | Residual | Sleep | Wake |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `--enforce-eager` | 9.277 | 0.529 | 8.748 | 0.529 | 2.31 s | 0.32 s |
| ACL graph | 9.473 | 0.725 | 8.748 | 0.725 | 2.43 s | 0.31 s |
| ACL graph + `sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` | 9.582 | 0.457 | 9.125 | 0.457 | 2.40 s | 4.01 s |

GiB except the latency columns; three back-to-back runs on the same die with the same 0.549 GiB baseline.

**Where the residual is.** In the ACL-graph case the 725 MiB decomposes as 419.2 MiB of inactive blocks in the `weights` pool, 292.0 MiB of ACL graph memory pool, 24.0 MiB of live default-pool tensors and <= 15 MiB of driver/CANN state. Extra cleanup removes the graph pool and the captured workspaces (0.268 GiB) and costs 13x wake-up latency.

**Five findings that change the plan.**

1. **The largest releasable item is pool waste, not graphs.** The `weights` pool is 1586.0 MiB reserved with 1166.8 MiB active, so 419.2 MiB (26%) is free blocks that `CaMemAllocator` cannot return: a pluggable pool has no `empty_cache` (the `TODO` at the end of `use_memory_pool`). It survives asleep in every configuration, including level 2, and it also inflates the level-1 CPU backup budget.
2. **The graph pool is never dropped.** `Platform._global_graph_pool` and `ACLGraphWrapper.graph_pool` keep the handle for the process lifetime; in ACL mode it is 292.0 MiB reserved with 0 active blocks while asleep. Extra cleanup releases the blocks behind it but not the handle itself.
3. **The existing self-report is blind.** `SleepWakeupManager.sleep()` logged `released HCCL and attention workspace memory: 0.000 GiB` in every run, although 0.268 GiB measurably comes back. It samples free memory around its own calls, before the allocator releases its cache. That is why the transaction starts with an accounting RPC (T0) and not with a release change.
4. **HCCL destroy returns ~0 MiB at TP=1.** `destroy_hccl()` destroys all 7 process groups at TP=1 and the driver free-bytes delta is 0 MiB. Expected at TP=1, unproven at scale: TP8/EP8 is where the upstream NCCL equivalent costs 1.26-1.64 GiB/GPU, so the flag cannot be recommended for those topologies before a two-node measurement.
5. **Untagged scratch is everywhere.** `attention/dsa_v1.py:1691-1719` (`_oproj_send_buf`/`_oproj_recv_buf`/`_oproj_rs_out_buf`), `attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py:648` and `:921`, `attention/context_parallel/dsa_cp.py:2244`, `attention/dsa_v41.py:601-605`, `ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py` and `distributed/weight_transfer/packed_tensor.py` (2x1 GiB HCCL or 1 GiB NPU IPC per rank) allocate into the default pool at init or at transfer time, where sleep cannot see them. They are too small to move the number on a dense 0.6B model; they are the reason the MoE and TP8 reference configurations are in the exit criteria.

**Not measured yet, and why.** MoE/EP workspaces (a MoE reference needs a model that fits a 64 GiB die; `Qwen3-30B-A3B` is ~61 GiB of bf16 weights, and no second free die was available for TP2), MTP/EAGLE draft buffers, HCCL at TP8/EP8, sparse-KV offload and KVPP arenas, Mooncake connector buffers, and the weight-transfer buffers under a live trainer. Those rows are written as "not measured yet" in the inventory rather than estimated.

The harness (device/pool/owner accounting plus a step-by-step release probe) is two files and is not committed; it can be attached to the first T0 PR.

## Overview

Allocate R3 capture buffers in the V2 runner's `profile_run()`, before KV-cache memory profiling and outside the weights memory pool. Adopt the minimal two-phase connector initialization from [aoshen02/vllm#189](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/189).

## Claims

- Create the AuxOutput connector and bind the capturer during profiling so automatic KV budgeting includes the persistent capture buffers and any monolithic routing sinks.
- Defer output storage until the resolved KV configuration is available, using `initialize_output_storage(kv_cache_config)` on the output TP rank. Retain connector construction as a fallback when normal profiling was skipped.
- Bump the Startup Plan schema to invalidate budgets recorded before this allocation moved into profiling.
- Keep GPUWorker, capturer binding, shutdown, and the existing R3 data-transfer paths unchanged from main. `profile_run()` creates the connector whenever aux output is enabled; this change does not guarantee repeated profiling is idempotent.

## Validation

Current head: `ab6712e28a0cd6ba437f1e0cace6097b136bcf8c`, based on main `df028dffa548710fb77320a5c08b87ae58757933`.

Checks completed locally:

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all six changed files: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main --check`: passed. All sixteen branch commits have DCO sign-off.
- Test tethering checks on the restored GPUWorker test file: passed; the two other test files passed this check in the preceding update.
- Three Startup Plan tests passed through an isolated pytest entry point that extracts the original test functions and fixture from `test_gpu_worker.py`, imports the real `startup_plan` module, and bypasses the global GPU conftest. They cover fingerprint sensitivity, budget application gates, and old-schema rejection. Hardware metadata is mocked by the existing fixture; cache JSON is actually written/read in temporary directories. This is not a full-suite pass.
- Negative control: setting the runtime schema to 1 caused the restored old-schema test to fail at the final budget assertion, as expected. Production files were not modified by this control.
- Four separate source-isolated runner/connector checks passed. They load actual definitions through AST, bypass Linux/GPU imports, and mock GPU helpers, covering profiling enabled/disabled, non-output TP rank and deferred storage.

The restored regression case saves a **1024-byte simulated budget**, changes the saved JSON schema to 1 while keeping its fingerprint, and verifies that the budget is not applied. It does not allocate GPU memory or measure R3 memory usage. Test changes are limited to `test_routed_experts_capture.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py` and `test_gpu_worker.py`; the sleep-mode test file matches main.

The normal command `pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k startup_plan` was attempted but collection was blocked by missing `uvloop` on Windows. Full `pre-commit run --files ...` remains blocked by Windows Git MSYS and hook-cache permission errors. Available checks were run directly. Mypy has no passing result.

GPU validation on this head is **not run**. R3 off/on KV-budget measurements, eager inference, sleep/wake, reload, CUDA Graphs, TP=2, explicit-KV-budget GPU behavior, Startup Plan first-boot/cache-hit behavior, sleep level 2, DP>1, and the monolithic sink GPU path remain unverified. No additional GPU E2E test is included in this diff. Earlier PR comments report results for older implementations and do not validate this head. No model-quality evaluation was run.

## Details

Previously `initialize_kv_cache()` constructed the connector after `determine_available_memory()` had fixed the automatic KV budget. The connector allocated persistent R3 GPU buffers too late to be accounted for.

The connector constructor now accepts the model and vLLM configuration, allocates the capturer and binds routing callbacks. Real KV initialization reuses that connector and calls `initialize_output_storage()` with the resolved layout; profiling KV initialization does not build the output data plane. Only the output TP rank builds the store and request buffer. The runner keeps the `None` fallback for initialization paths that skip normal profiling.

Production changes are limited to `gpu/model_runner.py`, `aux_output_connector/worker.py` and `startup_plan.py`. The earlier load-model initialization, ownership/unbind/rollback mechanisms and shutdown reordering have been removed. R3 SHM, prefix-cache, snapshots, asynchronous D2H and request-state behavior are unchanged.

Capture allocations remain resident outside the sleep allocator's weights/KV pools. Explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes` remains a manual budget and is not automatically reduced.

This updates the existing upstream PR and incorporates all three commits from aoshen02/vllm#189, retaining cherry-pick provenance. It does not create a competing upstream PR. AI assistance was used for implementation, checks and preparation. Full runtime/GPU validation and human review remain outstanding before merge.

```diff
-from functools import ...
+from functools import partial

```

`_CAPTURE_FN_OWNER_ATTR`, `_reject_second_capturer()`, rollback and unbind are unchanged.

### 2. Single `use_r3` guard

```diff
-        if (
-            self.use_v2_model_runner
-            and self.vllm_config.aux_output_config.enabled
-            and getattr(self.model_runner, "aux_output_connector", None) is not None
-        ):
+        use_r3 = self.use_v2_model_runner and self.vllm_config.aux_output_config.enabled
+        model_runner = cast("GPUModelRunnerV2", self.model_runner)
+        if use_r3 and model_runner.aux_output_connector is not None:
             raise RuntimeError(...)
...
-        if self.use_v2_model_runner and self.vllm_config.aux_output_config.enabled:
-            model_runner = cast("GPUModelRunnerV2", self.model_runner)
+        if use_r3:
             connector = get_aux_output_connector(self.vllm_config)
```

The duplicate check still runs before the weights pool, `model_runner.load_model()`, and any weight reload.

### `partial` equivalence

- Old closure called `capturer.capture(layer_id, topk_ids)`; new `partial(capturer.capture, layer_id)` binds the same bound method and prepends the same positional `layer_id`, so `capture_fn(topk_ids)` invokes `capturer.capture(layer_id, topk_ids)`.
- `functools.partial` instances support attributes, so `_CAPTURE_FN_OWNER_ATTR` is readable by `_reject_second_capturer()` and retains object identity.
- The installed object is the same object stored in `bindings`, so `restore_bindings()` identity checks and rebinding rejection are unchanged.
- Lifetime is unchanged: both forms hold a strong reference to the capturer until the callback is restored/removed.

### `load_model()` timing

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| R3 check | inline `v2 && r3` | `use_r3` once |
| Duplicate Connector | before pool, via `getattr` | before pool, direct attribute |
| Cast | inside second R3 block | before check (typing only) |
| Weights pool / load | after check | after check |
| Capturer create | after pool, before profiling | after pool, before profiling |
| EC / weight transfer / threads | after capture | after capture |

No runtime reordering beyond the cast, which is a no-op.

### Tests and checks

H20 CPU step on final head (CUDA-only `test_profile_cudagraph_memory_frees_throwaway_pool` deselected because the login node exposes a CUDA platform but no visible device):

```text
tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py                 74 passed  (includes new partial test)
tests/distributed/aux_output_connector                             68 passed
tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k "not test_memory_profiling"       3 passed, 1 deselected
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py                                 23 passed, 10 skipped
tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py    12 passed, 1 deselected
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
total                                                             180 passed, 10 skipped, 2 deselected, rc=0
```

New focused test: `test_make_capture_fn_uses_partial_and_keeps_owner` asserts the callback is `functools.partial`, the owner marker is the capturer, and `layer_id=1` writes to row 1 of the capturer buffer.

`run-precommit.sh <repo> 2d8d29a` -> `rc=0`: ruff check/format, typos, mypy (including the `partial` return type), test tethering, SPDX, forbidden imports, `torch.cuda` checks; DCO `ok`.

**GPU tests on `6295d99` are not executed**: all H20 GPUs are allocated; queued GPU job `2209` is estimated for 23:02 on 2026-10-23. This commit only changes callback construction and guard placement; the earlier GPU results for `4aa18a4` remain the reference for the unchanged normal path, and I am not presenting them as a new GPU run of `6295d99`.

### Correctness risks

- No behavior change from `partial`: it is callable with the same signature and supports dynamic attributes; no code inspects `__name__`/`__qualname__`.
- `cast` before the guard is typing-only; the V1 path short-circuits `use_r3` and never touches `aux_output_connector`.
- `use_r3` is consistent for the duration of `load_model()`, so the guard and capturer-creation branches cannot diverge.
- No change to R3 capture, two-phase Connector init, KV profiling, or shutdown.

issue.body:
## Overview

Allocate R3 capture buffers in the V2 runner's `profile_run()`, before KV-cache memory profiling and outside the weights memory pool. Adopt the minimal two-phase connector initialization from [aoshen02/vllm#189](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/189).

## Claims

- Create the AuxOutput connector and bind the capturer during profiling so automatic KV budgeting includes the persistent capture buffers and any monolithic routing sinks.
- Defer output storage until the resolved KV configuration is available, using `initialize_output_storage(kv_cache_config)` on the output TP rank. Retain connector construction as a fallback when normal profiling was skipped.
- Bump the Startup Plan schema to invalidate budgets recorded before this allocation moved into profiling.
- Keep GPUWorker, capturer binding, shutdown, and the existing R3 data-transfer paths unchanged from main. `profile_run()` creates the connector whenever aux output is enabled; this change does not guarantee repeated profiling is idempotent.

## Validation

Current head: `ab6712e28a0cd6ba437f1e0cace6097b136bcf8c`, based on main `df028dffa548710fb77320a5c08b87ae58757933`.

Checks completed locally:

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all six changed files: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main --check`: passed. All sixteen branch commits have DCO sign-off.
- Test tethering checks on the restored GPUWorker test file: passed; the two other test files passed this check in the preceding update.
- Three Startup Plan tests passed through an isolated pytest entry point that extracts the original test functions and fixture from `test_gpu_worker.py`, imports the real `startup_plan` module, and bypasses the global GPU conftest. They cover fingerprint sensitivity, budget application gates, and old-schema rejection. Hardware metadata is mocked by the existing fixture; cache JSON is actually written/read in temporary directories. This is not a full-suite pass.
- Negative control: setting the runtime schema to 1 caused the restored old-schema test to fail at the final budget assertion, as expected. Production files were not modified by this control.
- Four separate source-isolated runner/connector checks passed. They load actual definitions through AST, bypass Linux/GPU imports, and mock GPU helpers, covering profiling enabled/disabled, non-output TP rank and deferred storage.

The restored regression case saves a **1024-byte simulated budget**, changes the saved JSON schema to 1 while keeping its fingerprint, and verifies that the budget is not applied. It does not allocate GPU memory or measure R3 memory usage. Test changes are limited to `test_routed_experts_capture.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py` and `test_gpu_worker.py`; the sleep-mode test file matches main.

The normal command `pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py -k startup_plan` was attempted but collection was blocked by missing `uvloop` on Windows. Full `pre-commit run --files ...` remains blocked by Windows Git MSYS and hook-cache permission errors. Available checks were run directly. Mypy has no passing result.

GPU validation on this head is **not run**. R3 off/on KV-budget measurements, eager inference, sleep/wake, reload, CUDA Graphs, TP=2, explicit-KV-budget GPU behavior, Startup Plan first-boot/cache-hit behavior, sleep level 2, DP>1, and the monolithic sink GPU path remain unverified. No additional GPU E2E test is included in this diff. Earlier PR comments report results for older implementations and do not validate this head. No model-quality evaluation was run.

## Details

Previously `initialize_kv_cache()` constructed the connector after `determine_available_memory()` had fixed the automatic KV budget. The connector allocated persistent R3 GPU buffers too late to be accounted for.

The connector constructor now accepts the model and vLLM configuration, allocates the capturer and binds routing callbacks. Real KV initialization reuses that connector and calls `initialize_output_storage()` with the resolved layout; profiling KV initialization does not build the output data plane. Only the output TP rank builds the store and request buffer. The runner keeps the `None` fallback for initialization paths that skip normal profiling.

Production changes are limited to `gpu/model_runner.py`, `aux_output_connector/worker.py` and `startup_plan.py`. The earlier load-model initialization, ownership/unbind/rollback mechanisms and shutdown reordering have been removed. R3 SHM, prefix-cache, snapshots, asynchronous D2H and request-state behavior are unchanged.

Capture allocations remain resident outside the sleep allocator's weights/KV pools. Explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes` remains a manual budget and is not automatically reduced.

This updates the existing upstream PR and incorporates all three commits from aoshen02/vllm#189, retaining cherry-pick provenance. It does not create a competing upstream PR. AI assistance was used for implementation, checks and preparation. Full runtime/GPU validation and human review remain outstanding before merge.

Verified commit: `5eb420d8dbc64aad568068dfa0544c36204c001b`.

### GPU unit tests (H20-3e, 1 GPU)

Job `2062`, node `vllm-sgp-h20-01`. Compiled extensions reused from the Oct 21 wheel; the five modules changed by this PR are overlaid from the verified commit; test files are from the exact commit.

```text
tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py::test_memory_profiling                 1 passed
tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py                  70 passed
tests/distributed/aux_output_connector                               68 passed

tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py      13 passed
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
total                                                               180 passed, 1 skipped, rc=0
```

This includes the real-GPU memory-profiling test and the native-allocator cases that were skipped in the CPU-only step.

### End-to-end R3 on a tiny MoE

To exercise the full data path without a large checkpoint, I generated a random 2-layer Qwen3-MoE (hidden 128, 4 experts, top-2, 755k params) on the cluster and ran it with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `enable_return_routed_experts=True`, prefix caching, and `skip_tokenizer_init=True` (token-id prompts).

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| eager, R3 on | `routed_experts` shape `(7, 2, 2)`, dtype `uint8`, ids in `[0, 3]` |
| eager + `sleep(level=1)` / `wake_up()` | second generation after wake: shape `(7, 2, 2)`, ids in `[0, 3]` |
| cudagraph (`enforce_eager=False`), R3 on | `routed_experts` shape `(7, 2, 2)`, ids in `[0, 3]`; capture/replay with R3 callbacks active works |

The cudagraph case initially failed in `flashinfer.sampling` with `FileNotFoundError: ninja` (FlashInfer JIT build in the shared environment), unrelated to this change. Re-running with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` passed.

### KV-cache budget delta (end-to-end)

Same tiny model, `max_num_batched_tokens=131072`, eager, R3 off vs on:

| Run | `num_gpu_blocks` | block size | KV cache |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| R3 off | 4,519,296 | 16 | 68.96 GiB |
| R3 on | 4,518,016 | 16 | 68.94 GiB |
| **delta** | **1,280 blocks** | | **20 MiB** |

1,280 blocks x 16 KiB = 20 MiB. The capturer buffer itself is `131072 x 2 layers x 2 top-k x 4 B = 2 MiB`; the measured 20 MiB is PyTorch's caching-allocator large-pool segment (`kLargeBuffer = 20 MiB`) backing that allocation. The point of the test is that the allocation made before profiling is charged to non-KV memory, and `num_gpu_blocks` decreases accordingly. With `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` the same buffer fits in an existing allocator segment and the delta is hidden by 2 MiB block-count alignment, which is why the larger token budget was used.

### Environment caveats

- H20-3e, torch `2.13.0+cu130`, `vllm 0.32.1rc1.dev185+ge632d6643` compiled extensions.
- The wheel predates `SchedulerOutput.skip_drafts`, so for the e2e runs I overlaid **all 392 Python files that changed between the wheel commit and `5eb420d`** onto the wheel, keeping its compiled extensions. This is a source-overlay workaround, not a from-scratch build; the risk is limited to Python/compiled ABI drift, and no such mismatch appeared in the exercised path.
- The tiny model is random-weight; this validates the R3 data path and lifecycle, not model quality.

### Not verified

- Monolithic MoE `routing_sink` path end-to-end (the tiny Qwen3-MoE uses the Triton modular experts path; the sink path is covered by unit tests only).
- Weight reload / MoE kernel rebuild with R3, and multi-rank DP/TP capture.
- Large-model KV-budget delta (the unit accounting test plus the tiny-model delta cover the accounting mechanism).

Logs: `~/vllm-tasks/pr63237/logs/gpu-2062.log`, `e2e-2075.log`, `e2e2-2078.log`.

Latest PR head: `24f4aeb93f4b18c195035939029b0e3e841a41f0` (on top of `6295d99e6d`). DCO passes.

### Production diff

```diff

+

+                 partial(capturer.capture, module.layer_id))

 ...

-                _reject_second_capturer(routing_sink, "capture_fn")
             bindings.append((routed_experts, "routing_sink", routing_sink,
                              RoutedExpertsSink(..., capture_fn)))
-        elif isinstance(module.router, BaseRouter):
-            _reject_second_capturer(module.router, "capture_fn")
+        elif isinstance(module.router, BaseRouter):
             bindings.append((module.router, "capture_fn",
                              module.router.capture_fn, capture_fn))
```

Unbind/rollback is untouched:

- `bindings: list[tuple[Any, str, Any, Any]]` still records `(target, attr, previous, installed)`.
- `if getattr(target, attr, None) is not installed: continue` still skips callbacks replaced by other code.
- `BaseRouter.set_capture_fn(previous)` / `setattr(target, attr, previous)` unchanged.
- `try/except BaseException: restore_bindings(); raise` unchanged.
- Unbind remains idempotent.

`Any` remains imported because it is still used by the `bindings` tuple type. `functools.partial` remains.

### Why the ownership marker is no longer needed

The lower-level binding function is not the duplicate-prevention boundary:

1. `GPUWorker.load_model()` rejects a runner that already owns a connector before entering the weights pool.
2. `AuxOutputWorkerConnector.initialize_routed_experts_capturer()` is idempotent via `_capturer is not None`.
3. Weight reload, sleep/wake, and graph replay never call the binding function again.
4. Normal execution creates exactly one connector per model runner.

The marker only guarded direct repeated calls to `bind_routed_experts_capturer()`, which is outside this PR's supported API. That constraint is now documented at the function instead of enforced by a second ownership registry.

### `partial` equivalence

`partial(capturer.capture, layer_id)(topk_ids)` calls the same bound method with the same positional arguments as the old closure: `capturer.capture(layer_id, topk_ids)`. The same `partial` object is stored in `bindings` and installed on the target, so identity-based restore still identifies exactly this binding. No custom attributes are needed.

All three paths use it directly:

- Direct `RoutedExpertsCaptureSource`: appended inline.
- `BaseRouter`: `capture_fn = partial(...)`, then `set_capture_fn`.
- Monolithic MoE: `capture_fn = partial(...)` passed to `RoutedExpertsSink`.

### Explicit usage constraint

`bind_routed_experts_capturer()` does **not** support two active capturers nested on one model. Callers must unbind the current binding before binding another. Binding B over A would install B's callbacks; unbinding A then skips the replaced targets by identity, and unbinding B restores A's callbacks. Normal Worker/Connector paths cannot reach this state.

### Removed tests

Collection: **192 -> 188** (the expected four deletions).

- `test_make_capture_fn_uses_partial_and_keeps_owner` (helper and custom attribute are gone).
- `test_rebinding_model_to_another_capturer_is_rejected`.
- `test_rejected_rebind_leaves_new_targets_untouched`.
- `test_second_capturer_on_monolithic_sink_is_rejected`.

Kept: `test_rebind_after_unbind_uses_the_new_capturer` (bind A -> unbind A -> bind B -> capture with B), plus direct-source, BaseRouter, monolithic sink/kernel rebuild, non-R3 callback restoration, replacement-safe unbind, setter rollback, rollback-error preservation, buffer release, Connector/Worker duplicate-init guards, graph ordering, and profiling tests.

### Verification on the final head


Static checks: `run-precommit.sh <repo> 6295d99` -> `rc=0` (ruff check/format, typos, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, forbidden imports, `torch.cuda` checks); DCO `ok`.

### Correctness notes

- No new issue in the supported lifecycle: restore-by-identity, rollback, idempotent unbind, Worker/Connector single-owner checks all remain covered.
- The removed protection means a direct caller that skips unbind can stack bindings; that is now an explicit unsupported precondition, not a silent new feature.
